sentences.en: So Adam, where are we? I recorded this at the Ritz Carlton in Lower Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 所以 Adam，我们在哪？我在曼哈顿下城的丽思卡尔顿酒店录制的这个节目。

sentences.en: It's a black tie dinner. It was just a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 这是一场黑领带晚宴。就在几个星期前。

sentences.en: And you, by the way, are NPR's international business and economics correspondent?
sentences.zh: 顺便问一句，你是 NPR 的国际商业与经济记者吗？

sentences.en: That's right. I was there for my job. They're giving out awards for all these financial securities, including the one that nearly brought down the global financial system in the whole sub-prime mortgage crisis.
sentences.zh: 没错。我是为了工作在那里的。他们正在为所有这些金融证券颁奖，包括那个几乎拖垮全球金融系统和整个次贷危机的金融工具。

sentences.en: At this time, I'd like to ask all of our stars to please assemble over here on the left side of the stage-- This guy is a legend.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想请我们所有的明星到舞台左侧集合——这家伙是个传奇。

sentences.en: He's a granddaddy of our industry. I'm sitting at this dinner with Jim Finkel.
sentences.zh: 他是我们行业的元老。我正和 Jim Finkel 一起坐在这次晚宴上。

sentences.en: He's kind of nervous, because he's up for CDO of the year for the CDO he created, Monterey.
sentences.zh: 他有点紧张，因为他凭借自己创造的 CDO 产品 Monterey 入围了年度 CDO 的角逐。

sentences.en: Now, the CDO, that's what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 现在，CDO，这就是我们在讨论的东西。

sentences.en: That's the financial instrument that was central to this global credit crisis we're in.
sentences.zh: 这就是对我们身处的这场全球信贷危机起决定性作用的金融衍生品。

sentences.en: And they gave awards for this? These guys are giving each other awards for doing that?
sentences.zh: 他们竟然还为此颁奖？这些家伙竟然在为这种事互相颁奖？

sentences.en: Let me just say that they were aware that there's a certain irony, giving awards to the instrument that almost destroyed the world economy.
sentences.zh: 让我直说吧，他们也意识到给这个差点摧毁世界经济的金融工具颁奖具有某种讽刺意味。

sentences.en: And they did consider canceling this year.
sentences.zh: 他们确实考虑过今年取消颁奖。

sentences.en: But it's been a really tough year. It's been really gloomy for them.
sentences.zh: 但这一年真的很艰难。对他们来说实在是太阴暗了。

sentences.en: Honestly, I know this sounds-- I was really happy to see there were no major suicides, people weren't jumping off bridges, there weren't a lot of personal disasters.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我知道这听起来——我真的很高兴看到没有发生重大自杀事件，人们没有跳桥，也没有出现大量个人灾难。

sentences.en: Now that same week, a few days earlier, across the river in Brooklyn, I went to a completely different kind of gathering.
sentences.zh: 就在那个星期，几天前，在河对岸的布鲁克林，我去了另一个完全不同聚会。

sentences.en: It was not black tie. It was put on by the Neighborhood Assistance Corporation of America.
sentences.zh: 那不是黑领带晚宴。它是由美国邻里援助协会举办的。

sentences.en: It was people on the opposite side of the mortgage crisis, people facing foreclosure, trying to figure out how to keep their homes.
sentences.zh: 那是处于次贷危机对立面的人们，面临房屋被止赎的人们，他们正试图弄清楚如何保住房子。

sentences.en: I met this one guy, Richard. He's a marine.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了这个人，理查德。他是一名海军陆战队员。

sentences.en: He's this big guy, over six feet tall. And when he came back from Iraq a few years ago, he bought one of these fancy new mortgages with an adjustable rate.
sentences.zh: 他是个大个子，身高超过六英尺。几年前他从伊拉克回来后，买了一款这种带可调整利率的新潮抵押贷款。

sentences.en: Recently his rate reset. It has gone up by more than $2,000 a month.
sentences.zh: 最近他的利率重新调整了。每月多出了两千多美元。

sentences.en: And he has fallen behind on his payments.
sentences.zh: 而他的还款已经开始拖欠了。

sentences.en: It got to the point where-- one point, my son had $7,000 in a CD.
sentences.zh: 事情发展到——有一次，我儿子在存单里有 7,000 美元。

sentences.en: And I had to break it. And I mean that really hurt, because I was saving that money for his college.
sentences.zh: 我不得不把它取出来。我的意思是这真的很伤人，因为我是为他存大学学费的。

sentences.en: I mean, I put $2,000 back. But it's like you can't have a future.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我后来存回了 2,000 美元。但这感觉就像你无法拥有未来。

sentences.en: They put you in a situation where, after a while, you're going to fail.
sentences.zh: 他们把你置于这样一种境地：过一段时间后，你注定会失败。

sentences.en: It's hard. Now, it's clear that these two groups are connected, Jim at his black tie dinner and Richard the marine.
sentences.zh: 这太难了。现在，很明显这两群人是有联系的，参加黑领带晚宴的 Jim 和海军陆战队员理查德。

sentences.en: The sub-prime crisis has connected them.
sentences.zh: 次贷危机将他们联系在了一起。

sentences.en: Right, and I know that, basically, this is what sent you and one of the producers of our show, Alex Blumberg, on a big reporting mission these past few months.
sentences.zh: 对，我知道，基本上，这就是你和我们节目的制作人之一 Alex Blumberg 在过去几个月里进行伟大报道任务的原因。

sentences.en: You saw that, that there is this long chain of people that starts with these Wall Street guys and ends with people who stand to lose their houses.
sentences.zh: 你看到了，存在着这样一条长长的链条，从华尔街的这些家伙开始，到面临失去房子的普通人结束。

sentences.en: And all along that chain there were bankers, and brokers, and investors, and homeowners.
sentences.zh: 在这条链条的沿途，有银行家、经纪人、投资者和购房者。

sentences.en: And everybody along the chain kind of deluded themselves, thinking they could throw out the old rules of banking.
sentences.zh: 链条上的每个人都有些自欺欺人，以为他们可以抛弃传统的银行旧规则。

sentences.en: Right, in all the coverage of this, we hadn't heard that much from the people all along the chain.
sentences.zh: 对，在所有关于此事的报道中，我们并没有听到太多链条上各个环节的人的声音。

sentences.en: We wanted to know, what were they thinking when they were doing all this?
sentences.zh: 我们想知道，他们在做这一切的时候都在想什么？

sentences.en: And why did they think it would work? And simply, how did it all work?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们认为这行得通？简单来说，这一切到底是怎么运作的？

sentences.en: So, this is what we're devoting our program to today.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我们今天节目的主题。

sentences.en: From WBEZ Chicago, it's This American Life, distributed by Public Radio International.
sentences.zh: 来自芝加哥 WBEZ 电台，这是由美国公共广播电台发行的《This American Life》。

sentences.en: I'm Ira Glass. And today's show is a special co-production we're doing with NPR News, your place of employment, Adam.
sentences.zh: 我是 Ira Glass。今天的节目是我们与 NPR 新闻联合制作的特别节目，Adam，也就是你工作的地方。

sentences.en: Very proudly so. You and Alex Blumberg are going to be explaining step-by-step how this all worked.
sentences.zh: 我为此感到非常自豪。你和 Alex Blumberg 将一步一步地解释这一切是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And we will meet some of the people who created this economic disaster.
sentences.zh: 我们将见到一些一手制造了这场经济灾难的人。

sentences.en: And so let me turn the show over to the two of you, which is great for me, because I've pretty much lost my voice anyway.
sentences.zh: 所以，请容许我把节目交给你们两位，这对我来说太棒了，因为反正我的嗓子也差不多哑了。

sentences.en: And Alex Blumberg will kick things off.
sentences.zh: 接下来由 Alex Blumberg 拉开帷幕。

sentences.en: The thing that got me interested in all this was something called a NINA loan.
sentences.zh: 让我对这一切产生兴趣的是一种叫做 NINA 贷款的东西。

sentences.en: Back when the housing crisis was still a housing bubble, a guy on the phone told me that a NINA loan stands for no income no asset.
sentences.zh: 早在住房危机还是住房泡沫的时候，电话那头的一个家伙告诉我，NINA 贷款代表无收入无资产。

sentences.en: As in, someone will lend you a bunch of money without first checking to see if you have any income or any assets.
sentences.zh: 就像是，有人会在不事先核实你是否有任何收入或任何资产的情况下，借给你一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And it was an official loan product, like you could walk into a mortgage broker's office and they would say, well, we can give you a 30 year fixed rate, or we could put you in a NINA.
sentences.zh: 它是一种官方贷款产品，就像你走进一家抵押贷款经纪人的办公室，他们会告诉你，好吧，我们可以给你提供 30 年期固定利率，或者我们可以帮你办一笔 NINA 贷款。

sentences.en: He said there were lots of loans like this, where the bank didn't actually check your income, which I found confusing.
sentences.zh: 他说有很多这样的贷款，银行根本不核实你的收入，这让我感到很困惑。

sentences.en: And it turns out even the people who got them found them confusing.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，甚至连那些获得贷款的人也觉得很困惑。

sentences.en: For example, a guy I met named Clarence Nathan.
sentences.zh: 例如，我遇到过一个叫 Clarence Nathan 的人。

sentences.en: He worked three part-time, not very steady jobs, and made a total of $45,000 a year, roughly.
sentences.zh: 他做了三份兼职，工作不是很稳定，总共年收入大约 45,000 美元左右。

sentences.en: He got himself into trouble and needed money.
sentences.zh: 他陷入了困境，急需用钱。

sentences.en: So he took out a loan against his house, a big one.
sentences.zh: 于是他以房子作抵押贷了一笔款，数额很大。

sentences.en: Call it $540,000 for round figures. You basically borrowed $540,000 from the bank, and they didn't check your income?
sentences.zh: 按整数算大约是 540,000 美元。你基本上从银行借了 540,000 美元，而他们没有核实你的收入？

sentences.en: It's a no income verification loan. They don't call me up and say, how much money?
sentences.zh: 这是一笔无需收入证明的贷款。他们不会打电话问我，有多少钱？

sentences.en: They don't do that. I mean it's almost like you pass a guy in the street, and you say, will you lend me $540,000?
sentences.zh: 他们不这么做。我的意思是，这几乎就像你在街上和一个擦肩而过的人说，你能借给我 540,000 美元吗？

sentences.en: He says, well what do you do? Hey, I got a job.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，你是做什么的？嘿，我有工作。

sentences.en: OK. It seems as if it's that casual, even though there are a lot of papers that get filled out and stuff flies all over with the faxes and the emails, and all like that.
sentences.zh: 好的。虽然有很多文件需要填写，传真和电子邮件满天飞，诸如此类，但事情看起来就是这么随意的。

sentences.en: Essentially, that's the process.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这就是整个过程。

sentences.en: Would you have loaned you the money? I wouldn't have loaned me the money.
sentences.zh: 如果是你会借给自己这笔钱吗？我不会借给自己这笔钱。

sentences.en: And nobody that I know would have loaned me the money.
sentences.zh: 我认识的人里也没有谁会借给我这笔钱。

sentences.en: I mean, I know guys who are criminals that wouldn't lend me that money, and they'd break your kneecaps.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认识一些罪犯都不会借给我这笔钱，而他们可是会打断你的膝盖骨的。

sentences.en: So yeah, I don't know why the bank did it.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，我不知道为什么银行会这么做。

sentences.en: I'm serious. $540,000, a person with bad credit.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。540,000 美元，借给一个信用记录很差的人。

sentences.en: As it turns out, Clarence's friends, acquaintances and shadowy criminal contacts would have been right not to lend him the money.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，Clarence 的朋友、熟人和那些阴暗的犯罪黑幕联系人当初不把钱借给他才是对的。

sentences.en: By the time I talked to him, Clarence hadn't made a payment in almost a year, and his house was in the process of foreclosure.
sentences.zh: 当我跟他交谈时，Clarence 已经将近一年没有还款了，他的房子正处于被止赎的程序中。

sentences.en: And stories like this have been in the news for months.
sentences.zh: 像这样的故事在新闻里已经播了好几个月了。

sentences.en: And they often feature an innocent homeowner who was duped by a lying, greedy mortgage banker.
sentences.zh: 而且它们通常的主角都是一个被说谎、贪婪的房贷银行家欺骗的无辜房主。

sentences.en: Or if you're more of a Wall Street Journal editorial page type, an innocent mortgage banker who was duped by lying, greedy homeowner.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你更倾向于《华尔街日报》社论版的口味，那就是一个被说谎、贪婪的房主欺骗的无辜房贷银行家。

sentences.en: And no doubt, both categories exist. But Clarence's case is more nuanced, and much more common.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，这两类人都存在。但 Clarence 的情况更加微妙，也更为普遍。

sentences.en: Nobody came and told me a lie, and told me a story, and said, oh, just close your eyes, and all your problems will go away.
sentences.zh: 没有人来对我说谎，给我编故事，然后说，哦，闭上眼睛，你所有的麻烦都会消失的。

sentences.en: That wasn't the situation. The situation was that I needed the money.
sentences.zh: 情况并非如此。当时的情况是我确实需要钱。

sentences.en: And I'm not trying to absolve myself of anything.
sentences.zh: 我并不是想为自己开脱什么。

sentences.en: I had a situation. And I thought that I could do this, and then get out of it within six to nine months.
sentences.zh: 我遇到了情况。我当时以为我能搞定这笔钱，然后在六到九个月内脱身。

sentences.en: The six to nine month plan didn't work, so I'm stuck.
sentences.zh: 那个六到九个月的计划失败了，所以我被套牢了。

sentences.en: But if somebody had told me, you couldn't borrow the money, I probably would have had to do something else more drastic and dramatic, and not be in this situation now.
sentences.zh: 但如果有人当时告诉我，你根本不能借这笔钱，我可能不得不采取其他更极端、更剧烈的措施，而不是现在陷入这种境地。

sentences.en: The bank made an imprudent loan. I made an imprudent loan.
sentences.zh: 银行发放了一笔轻率的贷款。我申请了一笔轻率的贷款。

sentences.en: So the bank and I are partners in this deal.
sentences.zh: 所以银行和我在这笔交易中是合伙人。

sentences.en: This imprudent partnership is new. And it's at the heart of the current housing crisis.
sentences.zh: 这种轻率的伙伴关系是崭新的。而且它是当前住房危机的核心所在。

sentences.en: For most of the history of banking, bankers wouldn't have loaned Clarence their money either.
sentences.zh: 在银行业的绝大部分历史中，银行家同样也不会把钱借给 Clarence。

sentences.en: They didn't let people like Clarence near their money, in fact, people with part time employment and unpaid debts in their past.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们甚至不会让 Clarence 这样的人靠近他们的钱——那些身兼兼职工作且过去有未偿还债务的人。

sentences.en: And then suddenly in the early 2000s, everything changed.
sentences.zh: 然后突然在 2000 年代初，一切都变了。

sentences.en: Banking turned on its head and went out looking for partnerships with people like Clarence, loaning him half a million dollars without even checking to see if he had a job.
sentences.zh: 银行颠覆了常态，开始主动寻求与 Clarence 这样的人合作，甚至在不核实他是否有工作的情况下就借给他五十万美元。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well to help explain what happened here is my partner for the hour, Adam Davidson, the international business reporter for NPR.
sentences.zh: 为了解释发生了什么，这是我今天的搭档，NPR 国际商业记者 Adam Davidson。

sentences.en: Hey, Adam. Hey, Alex. How's it going? Good.
sentences.zh: 嘿，Adam。嘿，Alex。最近怎么样？很好。

sentences.en: I got your title right, right? Yes. Well, not exactly.
sentences.zh: 我没弄错你的头衔吧？是的。嗯，其实也不完全对。

sentences.en: Oh, what is it? It's international business and economics correspondent, actually.
sentences.zh: 哦，那是什麽？实际上是国际商业与经济 correspondent（记者）。

sentences.en: Oh, sorry. It actually sounds more impressive.
sentences.zh: 哦，抱歉。这听起来确实更厉害。

sentences.en: OK, so I guess the first thing we have to do is talk about the global pool of money, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我想我们首先要谈谈全球资金池，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, the global pool of money, that's where our story begins.
sentences.zh: 没错，全球资金池，我们的故事就是从那里开始的。

sentences.en: Most people don't think about it, but there's this huge pool of money out there, which is basically all the money the world is saving now-- insurance companies saving for a catastrophe, pension funds saving money for retirement, the Central Bank of England saving for whatever central banks save for, all the world's savings.
sentences.zh: 大多数人不会去想它，但存在着这样一个巨大的资金池，基本上就是全世界目前所有的储蓄——保险公司为灾难攒下的储蓄，养老基金为退休攒下的储蓄，英格兰中央银行为了中央银行储蓄的各种目的攒下的储蓄，也就是全世界所有的储蓄。

sentences.en: A lot of money, it's about 70 trillion. That's the head of capital market research at the International Monetary Fund, the place to go if you want to figure out how much money is in the world.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔巨款，大约有 70 万亿美元。这是国际货币基金组织资本市场研究负责人说的，如果你想搞清楚世界上到底有多少钱，找他们就对了。

sentences.en: So first off, how do we pronounce your name?
sentences.zh: 首先，你的名字该怎么发音？

sentences.en: That will probably take, if this goes on air, probably, that will take two minutes at least.
sentences.zh: 如果这期节目播出去，这大概，嗯，至少需要两分钟。

sentences.en: Ceyla Pazarbasioglu. I'm very impressed.
sentences.zh: Ceyla Pazarbasioglu。我印象深刻。

sentences.en: And by the way, before you finance enthusiasts start writing any letters, we do know that $70 trillion technically refers to that subset of global savings called fixed income securities.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，在你们这些金融爱好者写信反驳之前，我们确实知道 70 万亿美元在技术上是指全球储蓄中被称为固定收益证券的那一部分。

sentences.en: Everyone else can just ignore what I just said.
sentences.zh: 其他人可以忽略我刚才说的话。

sentences.en: Let's put $70 trillion in perspective. Do this.
sentences.zh: 让我们把 70 万亿美元放到宏观视角来看。这样做。

sentences.en: Think about all the money that people spend everywhere in the world, everything you bought in the last year, all of it.
sentences.zh: 想想全世界人们在所有地方花掉的所有钱，你在过去一年里买的所有东西，全部加起来。

sentences.en: Then add everything Bill Gates bought, and all the rice sold in China, and that fleet of planes Boeing just sold to South Korea, all the money spent in every country on Earth in a year.
sentences.zh: 再加上比尔·盖茨买的所有东西，中国卖掉的所有大米，波音公司刚卖给韩国的那批飞机，地球上每个国家在一年内花掉的所有钱。

sentences.en: That is less than $70 trillion, less than the global pool of money.
sentences.zh: 这加起来也还不到 70 万亿美元，比全球资金池还要少。

sentences.en: Wow. We're talking about a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 哇。我们谈论的是一笔巨款。

sentences.en: That is a lot of money. And that money comes along with armies of very nervous men and women watching over the pool of money.
sentences.zh: 那确实是一大笔钱。伴随着这笔钱的，是一支由极其焦虑的男男女女组成的庞大军队，时刻监管着这个资金池。

sentences.en: Investment managers, they don't want to lose a penny of that.
sentences.zh: 投资经理们，他们连一分钱都不想亏损。

sentences.en: They don't want to lose any of that money, and, even more so, they want to make it grow bigger.
sentences.zh: 他们不想损失任何资金，更重要的是，他们希望让资金增值。

sentences.en: But to make it grow, they have to find something to invest in.
sentences.zh: 但为了让资金增值，他们必须找到投资标的。

sentences.en: So, most of modern history, what they did was they bought really safe and, frankly, really boring investments like treasuries and municipal bonds, boring things.
sentences.zh: 因此，在现代历史的大部分时间里，他们的做法是购买真正安全、坦率地说也真的很无聊的投资，比如国债和市政债券，这些枯燥的东西。

sentences.en: But then, right before our story starts, something changed, something happened to that global pool of money.
sentences.zh: 但就在我们的故事开始之前，情况变了，全球资金池发生了一些变化。

sentences.en: This number doubled since 2000. In 2000 this was about $36 trillion.
sentences.zh: 这个数字自 2000 年以来翻了一番。在 2000 年，这大约是 36 万亿美元。

sentences.en: So it took several hundred years for the world to get to $36 trillion.
sentences.zh: 因此，全世界用了好几百年才积累到 36 万亿美元。

sentences.en: And then it took six years to get another $36 trillion.
sentences.zh: 然后仅仅用了六年时间就又增加了 36 万亿美元。

sentences.en: Yeah, there has been a very sharp increase.
sentences.zh: 是的，增长非常剧烈。

sentences.en: How does the world get twice as much money to invest?
sentences.zh: 世界是如何获得双倍的资金用来投资的？

sentences.en: There are lots of things that happen. But the main headline is that all sorts of poor countries became kind of rich, making things like TVs and selling us oil.
sentences.zh: 发生了很多事情。但核心大标题是，各种贫穷国家变得有点富裕了，他们通过制造电视机和向我们出售石油来赚钱。

sentences.en: China, India, Abu Dhabi, Saudi Arabia made a lot of money and banked it.
sentences.zh: 中国、印度、阿布扎比、沙特阿拉伯赚了大量的钱并存入了银行。

sentences.en: China, for example, has over a $1 trillion in its central bank.
sentences.zh: 例如，中国的中央银行拥有超过 1 万亿美元的外汇储备。

sentences.en: And there are office buildings in Beijing filled with math geniuses, real math geniuses, looking for a place to invest it.
sentences.zh: 北京的写字楼里挤满了数学天才，真正的数学天才，正在寻找投资的地方。

sentences.en: And the world was not ready for all this new money.
sentences.zh: 而世界并没有准备好迎接所有这些新资金。

sentences.en: There is twice as much money looking for investments, but there are not twice as many good investments.
sentences.zh: 寻找投资机会的资金翻了一番，但好的投资项目却没有翻番。

sentences.en: So that global army of investment managers was hungrier and twitchier than ever before.
sentences.zh: 因此，全球的那支投资经理大军比以往任何时候都更加饥渴、更加焦躁不安。

sentences.en: They all wanted the same thing, a nice, low-risk investment that paid some return.
sentences.zh: 他们都想要同一个东西：一份不错、低风险且能带来回报的投资。

sentences.en: But then something happened that makes matters worse.
sentences.zh: 但随后发生了一件事，让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: At this precise moment, one guy took one of that army's favorite investments and made it a lot less attractive.
sentences.zh: 就在这个精确的时刻，一个人把这支军队最喜欢的投资之一变得不再那么有吸引力了。

sentences.en: This is where we have to talk about Alan Greenspan, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们要谈论艾伦·格林斯潘（Alan Greenspan）的时候了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, we have to. All right. But I'm just going to promise people that is the only time you're going to hear Alan Greenspan in this story.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们必须谈。好吧。但我只想向听众保证，这是你在这个故事中最后一次听到艾伦·格林斯潘的名字。

sentences.en: So bear with us. All right. Here's one of his speeches that really drove that army of investment managers crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以请大家担待。好的。这是他的一篇真正让那支投资经理大军快要发疯的演讲。

sentences.en: The FOMC stands prepared to maintain a highly accommodative stance of policy for as long as needed to promote satisfactory economic performance.
sentences.zh: FOMC（联邦公开市场委员会）随时准备在必要的时间内保持高度宽松的政策立场，以促进令人满意的经济表现。

sentences.en: You might not believe me, but that little statement, that is central banker's speak for, hey, global pool of money, screw you.
sentences.zh: 你可能不相信我，但那个小小的声明，用中央银行家的黑话来讲就是：嘿，全球资金池，去你的吧。

sentences.en: Come on, that's not what he said. It is.
sentences.zh: 拜托，他才没这么说。就是这个意思。

sentences.en: I speak central banker. Believe me, that's what he said.
sentences.zh: 我懂中央银行家语言。相信我，他说的就是这个。

sentences.en: What he is technically saying is he's going to keep the fed funds rate-- that's when you hear, the fed interest rate-- at the absurdly low level of 1%.
sentences.zh: 他在技术上所说的是，他将把联邦基金利率——也就是当你听到所谓的联邦利率时——保持在 1% 的荒谬低水平上。

sentences.en: And that sends a message to every investor in the world, you are not going to make any money at all on US Treasury bonds for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 这向全世界的投资者传达了一个信息：在很长一段时间里，你们从美国国债上根本赚不到任何钱。

sentences.en: Go somewhere else. We can't help you. And so the global pool of money-- which does speak central banker.
sentences.zh: 去别的地方吧。我们帮不了你。因此，听得懂中央银行家语言的全球资金池——

sentences.en: They understood what he was saying-- they looked around for some low-risk high-return investment.
sentences.zh: 他们听懂了这话的含义——开始四处寻找一些低风险、高回报的投资。

sentences.en: And among the many things they put their money into, there was this one thing that they fell in love with.
sentences.zh: 在他们将资金投向的众多事物中，有这么一样东西让他们深深坠入爱河。

sentences.en: To get it, they called Wall Street, a guy like this.
sentences.zh: 为了得到它，他们打电话给华尔街，找了这样一个家伙。

sentences.en: My name is Mike Francis. During the beginning of the mortgage implosion, I was an employee, executive director at Morgan Stanley on the residential mortgage trading desk.
sentences.zh: 我叫 Mike Francis。在抵押贷款崩溃的初期，我是摩根士丹利住宅抵押贷款交易台的一名员工、执行董事。

sentences.en: Mike was one link in a chain that connected the global pool of money to its new favorite investment, residential mortgages, the US housing market, and guys like Clarence Nathan.
sentences.zh: Mike 是连接全球资金池与其新宠投资（住宅抵押贷款、美国房地产市场以及像 Clarence Nathan 这样的人）的一环。

sentences.en: Think how attractive a mortgage loan is to that $70 trillion pool of money.
sentences.zh: 想想看，对于那 70 万亿美元的资金池来说，抵押贷款是多么具有吸引力。

sentences.en: Remember, they're desperate to get any kind of interest return.
sentences.zh: 记住，他们极度渴望获得任何形式的利息回报。

sentences.en: They want to beat that miserable 1% interest Greenspan is offering them.
sentences.zh: 他们想要击败格林斯潘提供给他们的那悲惨的 1% 的利息。

sentences.en: And here are these homeowners paying 5%, 9% to borrow money from some bank.
sentences.zh: 而这里的这些房主却愿意支付 5%、9% 的利息向银行借钱。

sentences.en: So what if the global pool could get in on that action?
sentences.zh: 如果全球资金池能分一杯羹呢？

sentences.en: There are problems. Individual mortgages are too big a hassle for the global pool of money.
sentences.zh: 这里有问题。对全球资金池来说，单笔抵押贷款太麻烦了。

sentences.en: They don't want to get mixed up with actual people, and their catastrophic health problems, and their divorces, and all the reasons that might stop them from paying their mortgages.
sentences.zh: 他们不想与真人产生瓜葛，不想沾上他们灾难性的健康问题、离婚，以及所有可能阻止他们偿还房贷的原因。

sentences.en: So what Mike and his peers on Wall Street did, was to figure out a way to give the global pool of money all the benefits of a mortgage-- basically higher yield-- without all the hassle and risk.
sentences.zh: 因此，Mike 和他在华尔街的同僚们所做的，就是想出一个办法，把抵押贷款的所有好处——基本上是更高收益——在没有所有麻烦和风险的情况下打包给全球资金池。

sentences.en: So picture the whole chain. You have Clarence.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下整个链条。你有 Clarence。

sentences.en: He gets a mortgage from a broker. The broker sells the mortgage to a small bank.
sentences.zh: 他从经纪人那里获得抵押贷款。经纪人将抵押贷款卖给了一家小银行。

sentences.en: The small bank sells the mortgage to a guy like Mike at a big investment firm on Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 小银行再把抵押贷款卖给华尔街大型投资公司的 Mike 这样的家伙。

sentences.en: Then Mike takes a few thousand mortgages he's bought this way, he puts them in one big pile.
sentences.zh: 然后 Mike 把他通过这种方式买来的几千笔抵押贷款打包成一个大池子。

sentences.en: Now he's got thousands of mortgage checks coming to him every month.
sentences.zh: 现在他每个月都有成千上万张抵押贷款支票汇入。

sentences.en: It's a huge monthly stream of money, which is expected to come in for the next 30 years, the life of a mortgage.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔巨大的月度现金流，预计在未来 30 年（抵押贷款的生命周期）内源源不断地流入。

sentences.en: And he then sells shares of that monthly income to investors.
sentences.zh: 然后他将这部分月收入的份额卖给投资者。

sentences.en: Those shares are called mortgage-backed securities.
sentences.zh: 这些份额被称为抵押贷款支持证券（MBS）。

sentences.en: And the $70 trillion global pool of money loved them.
sentences.zh: 而 70 万亿美元的全球资金池对它们爱不释手。

sentences.en: It was unbelievable. I mean, we almost couldn't produce enough to keep the appetite of our investors happy.
sentences.zh: 这简直难以置信。我的意思是，我们几乎无法生产足够多的产品来满足投资者高涨的胃口。

sentences.en: More people wanted bonds than we could actually produce.
sentences.zh: 想要买债券的人比我们实际能生产的还要多。

sentences.en: That was our difficult task, was trying to produce enough.
sentences.zh: 我们面临的困难任务，就是努力生产出足够多的产品。

sentences.en: They would call and say, we're looking for more fixed rate.
sentences.zh: 他们会打电话来说，我们在寻找更多的固定利率产品。

sentences.en: What have you got? Do you have anything coming?
sentences.zh: 你们有什么？有什么新产品要出来吗？

sentences.en: What's going on? Tell us what you're trying to do.
sentences.zh: 情况怎么样？告诉我们你们打算做什么。

sentences.en: From our standpoint, it's like, there's a guy out there with a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 从我们的角度来看，就像是，外面有个家伙手里握着一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And we have got to find a way to become his sole provider of bonds, of mortgage bonds, to fill his appetite.
sentences.zh: 而我们必须想方设法成为他唯一的债券供应商，供应抵押贷款债券，以满足他的胃口。

sentences.en: And his appetite's massive.
sentences.zh: 而且他的胃口大得惊人。

sentences.en: The problem was, to make a mortgage-backed security, you needed mortgages.
sentences.zh: 问题是，要制造抵押贷款支持证券，你需要抵押贷款。

sentences.en: Lots of them. So for Mike Francis to satisfy this demand and take his quite hefty fee from the global pool of money, he needed to buy up as many mortgages as possible.
sentences.zh: 海量的抵押贷款。因此，为了满足这种需求并从全球资金池中抽取相当丰厚的手续费，Mike Francis 需要尽可能多地收购抵押贷款。

sentences.en: And to do that, he called a guy one link below him on this mortgage-backed security chain, a guy named Mike Garner, who worked at the largest private mortgage bank in Nevada, called Silver State Mortgage.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，他打电话给这条抵押贷款支持证券链条上比他低一环的家伙，一个名叫 Mike Garner 的人，他在内华达州最大的私人抵押贷款银行 Silver State Mortgage 工作。

sentences.en: And to give you a sense of how fast this business was growing, Mike Garner got into the mortgage business straight from his previous job as a bartender.
sentences.zh: 为了让你了解这个业务的发展速度有多快，Mike Garner 是直接从他之前调酒师的工作跳槽到房贷行业的。

sentences.en: One of my regulars, he actually hired me from the bar.
sentences.zh: 我的一个老顾客，他实际上直接从酒吧把我招了过去。

sentences.en: He just said he needed some guys, and if I was interested in working for him.
sentences.zh: 他只是说他需要几个人，问我有没有兴趣给他工作。

sentences.en: And then we started talking about how much I made and that.
sentences.zh: 然后我们开始谈论我赚多少钱之类的话题。

sentences.en: He beat me. He beat what I was making, so.
sentences.zh: 他给的薪水超过了我当时赚的，所以。

sentences.en: I didn't know anything about the mortgage business.
sentences.zh: 我对房贷行业一无所知。

sentences.en: I was as green as you could be. Mike Garner's job-- the guy in Nevada-- was to buy up individual mortgages, mainly from brokers, bundle 200 or 300 of them together, and then sell them up the chain to Wall Street, to guys like Mike Francis.
sentences.zh: 我当时菜得不能再菜了。Mike Garner 的工作——身处内华达州的那个家伙——就是收购个人抵押贷款，主要从经纪人那里收购，把 200 或 300 个打包在一起，然后往上游卖给华尔街，卖给像 Mike Francis 这样的家伙。

sentences.en: There's just too many Mikes here. I know.
sentences.zh: 这里的 Mike 实在太多了。我知道。

sentences.en: So many Mikes. There is actually just two Mikes.
sentences.zh: 太多的 Mike 了。其实这里面只有两个 Mike。

sentences.en: There's Mike Francis, the guy on Wall Street, and Mike Garner, the guy we're talking about now.
sentences.zh: 一个是身在华尔街的 Mike Francis，另一个是我们现在谈论的 Mike Garner。

sentences.en: He's in Nevada. He's in Nevada. Right. And in the beginning, he'd only buy mortgages that were pretty standard and pretty safe.
sentences.zh: 他在内华达州。他在内华达州。没错。一开始，他只买那些非常标准、非常安全的抵押贷款。

sentences.en: Mortgages where people had come up with a down payment and proven that they had a steady income and money in the bank.
sentences.zh: 也就是人们支付了首付，并证明自己有稳定收入和银行存款的抵押贷款。

sentences.en: And they sold so many of these mortgages that there came a point in 2003 where just about everybody who wanted a mortgage and was qualified to get one, had gotten one.
sentences.zh: 他们卖出了如此多的此类抵押贷款，以至于到 2003 年出现了一个转折点：几乎所有想要抵押贷款且有资格获得贷款的人，都已经贷到款了。

sentences.en: But the pool of money had just gotten started.
sentences.zh: 但资金池才刚刚开始发力。

sentences.en: They wanted more mortgage-backed securities.
sentences.zh: 他们想要更多的抵押贷款支持证券。

sentences.en: So Wall Street had to find more people to take out mortgages, which meant lending to people who never would have qualified before.
sentences.zh: 因此，华尔街不得不寻找更多的人来申请抵押贷款，这意味着要向那些以前绝无资格获得贷款的人发放贷款。

sentences.en: And so Mike Garner in Nevada noticed that every month the guidelines were getting a little looser.
sentences.zh: 于是，身处内华达州的 Mike Garner 注意到，每个月审批的标准都在变得越来越宽松。

sentences.en: Something called a stated income verified asset loan came out, which meant that people didn't have to provide a paycheck stub or W-2 form to get a loan as they had in the past.
sentences.zh: 一种名为“声明收入验证资产”的贷款出台了，这意味着人们不再需要像过去那样提供工资单或 W-2 表格来获得贷款。

sentences.en: They could simply state their income, as long as they showed that they had money in the bank.
sentences.zh: 他们只需声明自己的收入，只要能证明自己银行里有钱就行。

sentences.en: The next guideline lower is just stated income, stated assets.
sentences.zh: 比这低一档的标准就是单纯声明收入、声明资产。

sentences.en: That came out. So then you basically state what you make, and then you state what's in your bank account.
sentences.zh: 这随后也推出了。所以基本上你声明你赚多少钱，然后声明你银行账户里有多少钱。

sentences.en: They call and make sure that you work where you say you work.
sentences.zh: 他们会打电话核实你是否真的在你声称的地方工作。

sentences.en: And then an accountant has to say that for your field, it is possible to make what you say you make.
sentences.zh: 然后会计必须证明，就你的行业而言，赚取你所声称的收入是可能的。

sentences.en: But they don't have to-- they don't say what you make.
sentences.zh: 但他们不必——他们不用说你具体赚多少。

sentences.en: They just say, it's possible that he could make that.
sentences.zh: 他们只是说，他有可能赚到这个数。

sentences.en: If you could stop there for one second, it's just so funny that instead of just asking the people to prove what they make, there is this sort of theater in place of like, you have to find an accountant to say, yes this person who is sitting right in front of me, and who could very easily provide a W-2 form-- but we're not asking for a W2 form-- but we do want this accountant to say that, yeah, that person, what they're saying is possible in some universe.
sentences.zh: 如果你能停一下，这真的太滑稽了：不用让人们证明他们赚了多少钱，而是有一套戏码来代替，比如你必须找一个会计来背书，说“是的，这个坐在我面前的人，完全可以非常容易地提供一张 W-2 表格——虽然我们并没有要求提供 W-2 表格——但我们确实需要这位会计来说明，是的，这个人所说的话在某种宇宙中是有可能的。”

sentences.en: And I mean, loan officers would have an accountant that they could call up and say, can you write a statement saying that a truck driver can make this much money, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，贷款专员会有一个可以随时打电话的会计，说：“你能写一份声明，证明一个卡车司机能赚这么多钱，诸如此类的话吗？”

sentences.en: Then the next one came along. And it was no income verified asset.
sentences.zh: 然后下一个产品出现了。那是“无收入验证资产”贷款。

sentences.en: So you don't have to tell the people what you do for a living.
sentences.zh: 所以你甚至不需要告诉人们你靠什么谋生。

sentences.en: You don't have to tell the people what you do for work.
sentences.zh: 你不需要告诉别人你的工作是什么。

sentences.en: All you have to do is state that you have a certain amount of money in your bank account.
sentences.zh: 你唯一需要做的就是声明你的银行账户里有一定的存款。

sentences.en: And then the next one that came out is just no income no asset.
sentences.zh: 接下来推出的是无收入无资产贷款。

sentences.en: So you don't have to state anything. You just have to have a credit score and a pulse.
sentences.zh: 所以你什么都不用声明。你只需要有信用评分和一个心跳。

sentences.en: Actually that pulse thing, also optional, like this case in Ohio, where 23 dead people were approved for mortgages.
sentences.zh: 事实上，心跳这东西也是可选的，就像俄亥俄州的这个案例一样，23 个死人被批准了抵押贷款。

sentences.en: An interesting fact here. Mike Garner's bank did not care all that much how risky these mortgages were.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个有趣的事实。Mike Garner 的银行根本不在乎这些抵押贷款有多大风险。

sentences.en: This was a new era. Banks did not have to hold on to these mortgages for 30 years like they used to.
sentences.zh: 这是一个新时代。银行不再需要像过去那样把这些抵押贷款捏在手里 30 年。

sentences.en: They didn't have to wait and see if they'd be paid back.
sentences.zh: 他们不需要等待并观察这些贷款是否能被偿还。

sentences.en: Banks like Garner's would just own the mortgages for a month or two.
sentences.zh: 像 Garner 这样的银行只会持有这些抵押贷款一个月或两个月。

sentences.en: And then they sold them on to Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 然后把它们卖给华尔街。

sentences.en: And then Wall Street would sell them on to the global pool of money.
sentences.zh: 接着华尔街再把它们卖给全球资金池。

sentences.en: Which is how we get half million dollar no income no asset loans. --and loans to dead people.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们如何搞出五十万美元无收入无资产贷款的原因。——以及向死人发放贷款。

sentences.en: So there's this whole other thing going on as well.
sentences.zh: 所以当时还有另一件大事在发生。

sentences.en: Housing prices were rising fast. I think we all remember that.
sentences.zh: 房价飞涨。我想我们都还记得这一点。

sentences.en: Lots of people in the mortgage industry had this faith that housing prices in the US simply never go down.
sentences.zh: 房贷行业的很多人都有这样一种信念：美国的房价绝对不会下跌。

sentences.en: So from the bank's perspective, even if the worst happens and someone defaults, the bank would then own a house, which is now worth even more than what they gave out in the loan.
sentences.zh: 所以在银行看来，即使最坏的情况发生，有人违约了，银行将最终拥有一所房子，而这所房子的价值现在甚至比他们发放贷款时的金额还要高。

sentences.en: So all Mike cared about was whether or not his customers, the Wall Street investment banks, would buy those mortgages from him.
sentences.zh: 因此，Mike 唯一关心的是他的客户——华尔街投资银行——是否会从他手里买下这些抵押贷款。

sentences.en: And he was under pressure to approve more and more loans.
sentences.zh: 而且他承受着批准越来越多的贷款的压力。

sentences.en: Because other guys in his company-- the actual guys cruising strip malls all across Nevada buying mortgages from brokers-- their commission depended on selling more loans.
sentences.zh: 因为他公司的其他人——那些真正在内华达州各大购物中心穿梭、从经纪人那里购买抵押贷款的家伙——他们的佣金取决于卖出更多的贷款。

sentences.en: And occasionally those guys would hear about some loan that some other mortgage company offered that they weren't allowed to offer.
sentences.zh: 偶尔这些家伙会听到其他抵押贷款公司提供某种他们不被允许提供的贷款。

sentences.en: And they'd complain to Mike. Three of them would show up at your door first thing in the morning, and say, I lost 10 deals last week to Meritius Bank.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会向 Mike 抱怨。清晨一开盘，他们中就会有三个人冲进你的办公室，说：“我上周有 10 单生意被 Meritius 银行抢了。”

sentences.en: And they've got this loan. Look at the guidelines for this loan.
sentences.zh: “而且他们有这种贷款。看看这个贷款的审批标准。”

sentences.en: Is there any way we can do this, because we're losing deals left and right?
sentences.zh: “我们有没有办法做这个，因为我们的单子正在一单接一单地丢掉？”

sentences.en: Either they would find out who they were selling it to, or I'd get on the phone and start calling all these street firms or Countrywide and say, would you buy this loan?
sentences.zh: 要么他们会查出是谁在买这些贷款，要么我就拿起电话开始给所有这些华尔街公司或 Countrywide 打电话，问：“你们买这种贷款吗？”

sentences.en: And finally, you'd find out who's actually buying them and would say, yes.
sentences.zh: 最后，你会发现到底是谁在买，他们会说，是的。

sentences.en: So like, Merrill Lynch would say no, and Goldman Sachs would say no, and then you'd finally hit on somebody, and they would be like, yeah, we'll buy that loan.
sentences.zh: 比如，美林证券会说不，高盛会说不，然后你终于撞上了一个肯买的人，他们就会说，行，我们买这笔贷款。

sentences.en: Yeah, and then once I got a hit, then I'd call the other people back and say, listen, Bear Stearns is buying this loan.
sentences.zh: 是的，一旦我这边敲定了一家，我就会给其他人回电话，说：“听着，贝尔斯登正在买这种贷款。”

sentences.en: And I would like to give you the opportunity to buy these loans too.
sentences.zh: “我也想给你们一个机会购买这些贷款。”

sentences.en: And once one person buys them, usually all the rest follow suit.
sentences.zh: 一旦有一个人买单，通常其余的人都会效仿。

sentences.en: So, what were you thinking when you're turning around, and you're selling those to Wall Street?
sentences.zh: 那么，当你转过身把这些卖给华尔街的时候，你心里是怎么想的？

sentences.en: Were you ever thinking to yourself like, what are you guys doing?
sentences.zh: 你有没有在心里想过：你们这帮人在搞什么鬼？

sentences.en: Yeah, and my boss had been in the business for 25 years.
sentences.zh: 对，我的老板在这个行业干了 25 年。

sentences.en: And he hated those loans. He hated them.
sentences.zh: 他讨厌这些贷款。他恨透了。

sentences.en: And he used to rant and just say, it makes me sick to my stomach the kind of loans that we do.
sentences.zh: 他经常怒气冲冲地说，我们做的这种贷款让我感到胃里翻江倒海。

sentences.en: And he fought the owners and the sales force, tooth and neck, about these guidelines.
sentences.zh: 他为了这些审批标准，跟老板和销售团队进行了殊死搏斗。

sentences.en: And we got the same answer every time. Nope.
sentences.zh: 而我们每次得到的回答都是一样的。不行。

sentences.en: Other people are offering it. We're going to offer it too.
sentences.zh: 别人都在提供这种贷款。我们也要提供。

sentences.en: We're going to get more market share this way.
sentences.zh: 我们要用这种方法获得更多的市场份额。

sentences.en: House prices are booming. Everything's going to be good.
sentences.zh: 房价正在蓬勃发展。一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: And the company was just rolling in the cash.
sentences.zh: 而且公司当时正在大把大把地数钱。

sentences.en: I mean, the owners and the production staff were just raking it in.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，老板和生产人员简直是在疯狂捞钱。

sentences.en: At the height, I was making between $75,000 and $100,000 a month.
sentences.zh: 在巅峰时期，我每月的收入在 75,000 到 100,000 美元之间。

sentences.en: This is Glen Pizzolorusso, who was an area sales manager at an outfit called WMC Mortgage in upstate New York.
sentences.zh: 这是 Glen Pizzolorusso，他当时是纽约州北部一家名为 WMC Mortgage 的公司的区域销售经理。

sentences.en: And just to repeat, he said $75,000 to a $100,000 a month.
sentences.zh: 再重复一遍，他说的是每月 75,000 到 100,000 美元。

sentences.en: That's over a $1 million a year. Glen was just out of college.
sentences.zh: 那是年薪超过 100 万美元。Glen 当时刚大学毕业。

sentences.en: His job was a lot like Mike Garner's. He's the same link in the chain.
sentences.zh: 他的工作和 Mike Garner 的很像。他们在链条上的位置是一样的。

sentences.en: And Glen loved his job. What was that movie, Boiler Room?
sentences.zh: 而且 Glen 非常热爱他的工作。那部电影叫什么来着，《开锅》（Boiler Room）？

sentences.en: Did you ever see that movie? That's what it was like.
sentences.zh: 你看过那部电影吗？当时的情形就像那样。

sentences.en: I mean, it was the coolest thing ever. Just cubicle, cubicle, cubicle for 150,000 square feet.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那简直是最酷的事情。150,000 平方英尺的空间里全是一个接一个的格子间。

sentences.en: The ceilings were probably 25, 30 feet ceilings.
sentences.zh: 天花板大概有 25、30 英尺高。

sentences.en: The elevator had this big graffiti painting on it that was awesome.
sentences.zh: 电梯上有一幅很酷的大涂鸦画。

sentences.en: A graffiti painting, meaning like, that had been there since before you guys moved in?
sentences.zh: 涂鸦画，意思是，那是你们搬进去之前就有的吗？

sentences.en: So they had not done any amenities to this place?
sentences.zh: 所以你们没有对这个地方做任何装修或配套设施吗？

sentences.en: No, it was just a big, open space. And it was awesome.
sentences.zh: 不，它只是一个巨大的开放空间。而且太酷了。

sentences.en: We lived mortgage. That's what we did. That's all we did.
sentences.zh: 我们的生命里只有房贷。这就是我们所做的一切。这就是我们做的全部事情。

sentences.en: All of us, we just lived it. This deal, that deal, what's going on here?
sentences.zh: 我们所有人，都沉浸其中。这笔交易，那笔交易，这里发生了什么？

sentences.en: How are we going to get this one funded?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么把这一单搞定放款？

sentences.en: What's the problem with this one? I mean, you get there, and that's all everybody is talking about.
sentences.zh: 这一单有什么问题？我的意思是，你一到那儿，每个人谈论的就只有这些。

sentences.en: And when Glenn wasn't working, he was doing his next favorite thing, spending, preferably, in the company of-- and this is his term-- B-list celebrities.
sentences.zh: 当 Glen 不工作的时候，他就在做他第二件最喜欢的事：花钱，最好是在——用他的话说——B 级名人的陪伴下进行。

sentences.en: We would roll up to Marquee at midnight, with a line 500 people deep out front.
sentences.zh: 我们在午夜时分开车抵达 Marquee 夜店，门外排着长达 500 人的队伍。

sentences.en: Walk right up to the door. Give me my table.
sentences.zh: 径直走到门前。把我的桌子给我。

sentences.en: We're sitting next to Tara Reid and a couple of her friends.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在 Tara Reid 和她的几个朋友旁边。

sentences.en: Christina Aguilera was doing a-- whatever, I'm Christina Aguilera.
sentences.zh: Christina Aguilera 当时在进行一场——管他呢，我是 Christina Aguilera。

sentences.en: I'm going to get up and sing. So Christina Aguilera and all her people are there.
sentences.zh: 我要起来唱歌。所以 Christina Aguilera 和她的一帮人都在那儿。

sentences.en: Who else was there? Cuba Gooding and that kid from Filthy Rich: Cattle Drive.
sentences.zh: 还有谁在那儿？Cuba Gooding 和《Filthy Rich: Cattle Drive》里的那个小孩。

sentences.en: What was that kid's name? Fabian We ordered, probably, three or four bottles of Cristal at $1,000 a bottle.
sentences.zh: 那个小孩叫什么名字？Fabian。我们大概点了三、四瓶 Cristal 香槟，每瓶 1,000 美元。

sentences.en: They bring it out. They are walking through the crowd.
sentences.zh: 他们把酒端上来。他们穿过人群。

sentences.en: They hold the bottles over their head.
sentences.zh: 他们把酒瓶举过头顶。

sentences.en: The little cocktail waitresses, so you order four bottles of those, they're walking through the crowd of people.
sentences.zh: 那些小鸡尾酒女服务员，当你点四瓶这种酒时，她们会端着穿过人群。

sentences.en: Everybody is like, whoa, who's the cool guys?
sentences.zh: 每个人都在想：哇，这几个酷哥是谁？

sentences.en: Well, we were the cool guys. You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们就是那些酷哥。你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: They gave me a black card. This little card with my name on it.
sentences.zh: 他们给了我一张黑卡。这张印着我名字的小卡片。

sentences.en: There's probably like 10 of them in existence.
sentences.zh: 世界上大概只有 10 张左右吧。

sentences.en: And that meant that I just spent way too much money there.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我在那里花的钱远远超出了正常范畴。

sentences.en: Glen had five cars, a $1.5 million vacation house in Connecticut, and a penthouse that he rented in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: Glen 拥有五辆汽车、价值 150 万美元的康涅狄格州度假屋，以及他在曼哈顿租的一套顶层公寓。

sentences.en: And he made all this money making very large loans to very poor people with bad credit.
sentences.zh: 而他赚到所有这些钱，是通过向信用极差的极穷困人群发放数额巨大的贷款来实现的。

sentences.en: We looked at loans, these people didn't have a pot to piss in.
sentences.zh: 我们审视过一些贷款，这些人连个撒尿的盆都没有。

sentences.en: I mean, they could barely make the car payment, and now we're giving them a $300,000 to $400,000 house.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们几乎连汽车贷款都快还不起了，而我们现在却要给他们一套 300,000 到 400,000 美元的房子。

sentences.en: But Glen didn't worry about whether these loans were good either.
sentences.zh: 但 Glen 同样不担心这些贷款质量是否过关。

sentences.en: That was someone else's problem. And this way of thinking thrived at every step of this mortgage security chain.
sentences.zh: 那是别人的问题。这种思维方式在这个抵押贷款证券链条的每一个环节都大行其道。

sentences.en: A guy like Mike Francis from Morgan Stanley, he told me he bought loans, lots of loans, from Glen's company.
sentences.zh: 像摩根士丹利的 Mike Francis 这样的人，他告诉我他从 Glen 的公司买入了贷款，大量的贷款。

sentences.en: And he knew in his gut that they were bad loans, like these NINA loans.
sentences.zh: 他内心里很清楚这些都是烂贷款，比如这些 NINA 贷款。

sentences.en: No income no asset loans, that's a liar's loan.
sentences.zh: 无收入无资产贷款，那就是骗子贷款。

sentences.en: We are telling you to lie to us, effectively.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上是在告诉你们对我们撒谎。

sentences.en: I mean, we're hoping you don't lie, but-- tell us what you make.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们希望你们不要撒谎，但是——告诉我们你赚多少钱。

sentences.en: Tell us what you have in the bank. But we're not going to actually verify it?
sentences.zh: 告诉我们在银行里有多少钱。但我们其实并不会去核实？

sentences.en: We're setting you up to lie. Something about that transaction feels very wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们在诱导你们撒谎。这种交易感觉非常不对劲。

sentences.en: It felt very wrong way back when. And I wish we had never done it.
sentences.zh: 早在当时这就让人感觉非常不对劲。我真希望我们从未做过。

sentences.en: Unfortunately what happened, we did it because everybody else was doing it.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我们做了，因为其他人都在这样做。

sentences.en: It's easy to ignore your gut fear when you're making a fortune in commissions.
sentences.zh: 当你通过赚取巨额佣金发家致富时，很容易忽视内心深处的恐惧。

sentences.en: But Mike had other help in rationalizing what he was doing, technological help.
sentences.zh: 但 Mike 在合理化自己的行为方面得到了其他帮助——技术上的帮助。

sentences.en: Mike sat at a desk with six computer screens connected to millions of dollars worth of fancy analytic software designed by brilliant Ivy League graduates hired by his firm.
sentences.zh: Mike 的办公桌上摆着六台电脑屏幕，连接着价值数百万美元的精美分析软件，这些软件由他的公司雇佣的才华横溢的长春藤盟校毕业生设计。

sentences.en: And this software analyzed all the loans in all the pools that Mike bought and then sold.
sentences.zh: 这个软件分析了 Mike 买入并随后卖出的所有池子里的所有贷款。

sentences.en: And the software, the data, didn't seem worried at all.
sentences.zh: 而软件和数据看起来一点也不让人担心。

sentences.en: All the data that we had to review, to look at, on loans that were in production, that were years old, was positive.
sentences.zh: 我们必须审查的所有数据、查看的所有关于正在生产的、已经存在多年的贷款的数据，都是积极的。

sentences.en: They performed very well. All those factors, when you look at all the pieces and parts, and you say, well, a 90% no income loan three years ago is performing amazingly well.
sentences.zh: 它们的表现非常好。所有这些因素，当你审视所有的细枝末节时，你会说，好吧，三年前 90% 的无收入贷款表现得好得惊人。

sentences.en: It has a little bit of risk. Instead of defaulting 1 and 1/2% of the time, it defaults 3 and 1/2% of the time.
sentences.zh: 它有一点风险。违约率不是正常的 1.5%，而是变成了 3.5%。

sentences.en: Well, that's not so bad. If I'm an investor buying that, if I get a little bit of additional return, I'm fine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那也没那么糟。如果我是购买这种产品的投资者，如果我能获得一点点额外的回报，我完全可以接受。

sentences.en: Wait, Alex, I want step in here, because this is a very important piece of tape.
sentences.zh: 等等，Alex，我想插一句，因为这是一段非常重要的录音。

sentences.en: A big part of this whole story, the whole crisis, is that a lot of really smart people, people who knew better, fooled themselves with this data.
sentences.zh: 整个故事、整场危机的一个重要部分是，许多非常聪明、本该明白事理的人，却被这些数据给愚弄了。

sentences.en: It was the triumph of data over common sense.
sentences.zh: 这是数据对常识的胜利。

sentences.en: Can you play that tape again? Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 你能再播放一遍那段录音吗？没问题。

sentences.en: Here you go. All the data that we had to review, to look at, on loans that were in production, that were years old, was positive.
sentences.zh: 给你。我们必须审查的所有数据、查看的所有关于正在生产的、已经存在多年的贷款的数据，都是积极的。

sentences.en: As we now know, they were using the wrong data.
sentences.zh: 正如我们现在所知，他们当时使用的是错误的数据。

sentences.en: They looked at the recent history of mortgages and saw that the foreclosure rate is generally below 2%.
sentences.zh: 他们查看了抵押贷款的近期历史，发现止赎率通常低于 2%。

sentences.en: So they figured absolute worst-case scenario, the foreclosure rate might go to 8% or 10% or even 12%.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为绝对最坏情况下的场景是，止赎率可能会上升到 8%、10% 甚至 12%。

sentences.en: But the problem with that is that there were all these new kinds of mortgages given out to people who never would have gotten them before.
sentences.zh: 但其中的问题在于，有各种各样全新的抵押贷款发放给了以前绝不可能获得贷款的人。

sentences.en: So the historical data was irrelevant. Some mortgage pools today are expected to go beyond 50% foreclosure rates.
sentences.zh: 因此历史数据毫无参考价值。如今的一些抵押贷款池预计将出现超过 50% 的止赎率。

sentences.en: To be fair, they knew there were risks. But investors have a system to assesses those risks.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，他们知道存在风险。但投资者有一套评估这些风险的系统。

sentences.en: They have the special companies, credit rating agencies, Moody's, Standard & Poor's, Fitch.
sentences.zh: 他们有专门的公司，即信用评级机构：穆迪、标准普尔、惠誉。

sentences.en: Their job, their main job, is to assess risk for Wall Street and the global pool of money.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作，主要工作，就是为华尔街和全球资金池评估风险。

sentences.en: They rate every kind of bond according to its risk.
sentences.zh: 他们根据风险对每一种债券进行评级。

sentences.en: AAA is the safest. Then there is AA, A, all the way down to B and below.
sentences.zh: AAA 是最安全的。然后是 AA、A，一直往下到 B 级及以下。

sentences.en: And that's all most investors look at that, that letter grade.
sentences.zh: 大多数投资者看的也就是这些字母评级。

sentences.en: They trust the credit rating agencies. And these agencies blessed most of these mortgage-backed securities, gave them AAA ratings, which means they were considered as safe as a US government bond.
sentences.zh: 他们信任信用评级机构。而这些机构对大多数抵押贷款支持证券给予了祝福，给它们评了 AAA 级，这意味着它们被认为和美国政府债券一样安全。

sentences.en: This was the magic of the whole system. You could take a pool of thousands of risky mortgages and create a security that was called, money good, as safe as any investment out there.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个系统的魔力所在。你可以把成千上万笔有风险的抵押贷款打包成一个池子，创造出一种被称为“资金绝对安全”的证券，其安全性不亚于市面上的任何投资。

sentences.en: At least that's what people thought. We now know that those agencies relied on the wrong data, that same historic data that had nothing to do with these new kinds of mortgages.
sentences.zh: 至少人们当时是这么认为的。我们现在知道，那些评级机构依赖的是错误的数据，也就是那些与这些新型抵押贷款毫无关系的同一批历史数据。

sentences.en: And then, things got even worse. The thing that took this problem and turned it into a crisis was something else that was new, something called a collateralized debt obligation, a CDO.
sentences.zh: 然后，情况变得更糟了。把这个问题演变成危机的是另一件新鲜事，一种被称为债务担保凭证（CDO）的东西。

sentences.en: And that brings us back to the guy we met at the awards dinner in the beginning, Jim Finkel.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了我们在开头的颁奖晚宴上遇到的那个家伙，Jim Finkel。

sentences.en: Well, we're heading to the trading floor of Dynamic Credit, where we have all of our mortgage and CDO analysts, our head trader, our CIO-- Jim Finkel runs this CDO shop, Dynamic Credit.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们要前往 Dynamic Credit 的交易大厅，那里有我们所有的抵押贷款和 CDO 分析师、首席交易员、首席投资官——Jim Finkel 经营着这家 CDO 公司，Dynamic Credit。

sentences.en: It takes up three modified apartments on the Upper East Side of Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 它占据了曼哈顿上东区三套改造过的公寓。

sentences.en: The trading room is like a factory floor for CDOs.
sentences.zh: 交易室就像是制造 CDO 的工厂车间。

sentences.en: It's where they make the things. This is what it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们制造这些东西的地方。听起来就是这样的。

sentences.en: Maybe factory is the wrong term. But this is where he makes CDOs.
sentences.zh: 也许“工厂”这个词用得不对。但这就是他制造 CDO 的地方。

sentences.en: But what is a CDO? He shows us on a computer screen.
sentences.zh: 但什么是 CDO？他在电脑屏幕上向我们展示了这一点。

sentences.en: I'm going to show you-- here's our deal, Monterey.
sentences.zh: 我要给你展示一下——我们的交易是这样的，Monterey。

sentences.en: To start with, every CDO has its own name.
sentences.zh: 首先，每个CDO都有自己的名字。

sentences.en: Finkel loves his country house in the Berkshires, so he always names CDOs after towns in western Mass, like Monterey.
sentences.zh: Finkel非常喜欢他在伯克希尔的乡村别墅，所以他总是用马萨诸塞州西部的城镇来给CDO命名，比如Monterey。

sentences.en: Monterey CDO Limited, we had a 189 assets in Monterey.
sentences.zh: Monterey CDO Limited，我们在Monterey有189项资产。

sentences.en: So that's 189 pools? --189 tranches of different mortgage-backed pools.
sentences.zh: 所以那是189个资产池？——189个不同抵押贷款支持资产池的分档。

sentences.en: Let's translate some of that. A mortgage-backed security, you remember, is a pool of thousands of different mortgages.
sentences.zh: 我们来解释一下其中的一些概念。你还记得，抵押贷款支持证券是由成千上万笔不同的抵押贷款组成的资产池。

sentences.en: These are all put together and divided into different slices.
sentences.zh: 这些贷款被组合在一起，并被分割成不同的切片。

sentences.en: Tranche is just French for slice. Some of these slices are risky and some are not.
sentences.zh: Tranche在法语里就是切片的意思。这些切片中，有些是有风险的，有些则没有。

sentences.en: OK, a CDO is a pool of these tranches, a pool of pools.
sentences.zh: 好了，CDO就是这些分档的集合，也就是资产池的资产池。

sentences.en: And Jim and most companies like his weren't buying the top rated tranches, the safest ones, the AAAs.
sentences.zh: Jim以及大多数像他这样的公司，买的并不是评级最高的分档、最安全的那部分，也就是AAA级。

sentences.en: They were buying the lower rated stuff, the high risk stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们买的是评级较低的东西，高风险的东西。

sentences.en: Jim's company bought tranches that came from Glen Pizzolorusso's company, the guy who hung out at nightclubs with B-list celebrities, the guy who said he was selling mortgages to people who didn't have a pot to piss in.
sentences.zh: Jim的公司买的分档来自于Glen Pizzolorusso的公司，就是那个整天跟二线名人混夜店的家伙，那个说自己把房贷卖给连饭碗都买不起的人的家伙。

sentences.en: There is another term the industry uses.
sentences.zh: 业内还有另一个术语。

sentences.en: This is not a joke. They call these lower rated tranches, toxic waste.
sentences.zh: 这不是开玩笑。他们把这些低评级的分档叫做“有毒废料”。

sentences.en: They are so high risk, they're toxic. So basically Adam, a CDO is sort of a financial alchemy, right?
sentences.zh: 它们的风险太高了，简直有毒。所以基本上，Adam，CDO有点像是一种金融炼金术，对吧？

sentences.en: Jim takes this toxic stuff, these low-rated high-risk tranches, puts them all together, re-tranches them, and presto.
sentences.zh: Jim把这些有毒的东西、这些低评级高风险的分档收集起来，重新分档，然后——变戏法似地。

sentences.en: He has a CDO whose top tranche is rated AAA, rock solid, good as money.
sentences.zh: 他搞出了一个CDO，其最顶层的分档评级为AAA，稳如磐石，跟钱一样硬挺。

sentences.en: If this seems too good to be true to you, you're in good company.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这好得令人难以置信，那说明你并不孤单。

sentences.en: Guys like billionaire investor Warren Buffett said the very logic was ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 像亿万富翁投资者沃伦·巴菲特这样的人就说，这种逻辑简直荒谬。

sentences.en: But back in 2005, 2006, the global pool of money, they couldn't get enough of these things.
sentences.zh: 但在2005年、2006年，全球资金池对这些东西简直趋之若鹜。

sentences.en: And the CDO industry was facing the same pressures everyone else was at every other step of this chain, to loosen their standards, to make CDOs out of lower and lower rated tranches.
sentences.zh: CDO行业面临着这条链条上其他所有环节所面临的相同压力：放松标准，用评级越来越低的分档来制造CDO。

sentences.en: This is Jim's partner, Tonko Gast. Actually, in 2005 already, we had an internal debate here, because there were two banks coming to us saying, why don't you do a deal with us, BBB securities, and you get paid $1 million in management fees per year?
sentences.zh: 这是Jim的合伙人Tonko Gast。其实早在2005年，我们内部就有一场辩论，因为当时有两家银行来找我们，说，你们为什么不跟我们做一笔交易，买BBB级的证券，每年你们能拿到100万美元的管理费？

sentences.en: Very clear, just like that, in 2005.
sentences.zh: 非常明确，就这么直接，在2005年。

sentences.en: And we declined those deals. We said that we just don't believe that those BBB RMBS assets are money-good.
sentences.zh: 我们拒绝了这些交易。我们当时说，我们就是不相信那些BBB级的RMBS资产能够保证兑付。

sentences.en: We don't think they are well underwritten.
sentences.zh: 我们认为它们的承销审核并不过关。

sentences.en: And we think if we do a CDO of those, that's going to blow up completely.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得如果我们拿那些东西去做个CDO，那绝对会彻底炸雷。

sentences.en: We were a little early in '05 by not wanting to do those deals.
sentences.zh: 我们2005年时拒绝做这些交易，确实有点操之过急了。

sentences.en: And people were laughing at us, to be honest, to say, well, you're crazy.
sentences.zh: 说实话，当时人们都在笑话我们，说，你们疯了吧。

sentences.en: You're hurting your business. Why don't you want to make-- per deal, you could make $1 million a year.
sentences.zh: 你们在跟自己的生意过不去。一笔交易每年就能赚100万美元，你们为什么不干？

sentences.en: Did someone do that deal? Absolutely. Everybody.
sentences.zh: 有没有人接这笔交易？当然有。所有人都在做。

sentences.en: Not everybody, but a lot of people did.
sentences.zh: 也不是所有人，但很多人都做了。

sentences.en: Coming up, how $5 million can get you into $100 million worth of trouble.
sentences.zh: 接下来的节目中，500万美元如何让你陷入价值1亿美元的麻烦中。

sentences.en: In a minute, from Chicago Public Radio and Public Radio International when our program continues.
sentences.zh: 稍后，节目继续，我们将为您播出由芝加哥公共广播电台和国际公共广播电台联合制作的节目。

sentences.en: Well, it's This American Life. I'm Ira Glass.
sentences.zh: 这里是《美国生活》（This American Life）。我是伊拉·格拉斯（Ira Glass）。

sentences.en: And although I feel fine, I have lost my voice this week.
sentences.zh: 虽然我感觉身体无大碍，但我这周嗓子哑了。

sentences.en: Today's show, a special co-production with NPR News, a step-by-step look at what exactly happened during the sub-prime mortgage crisis.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目是与NPR新闻联合制作的特别节目，我们将一步步剖析次贷危机期间到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: One of our producers, Alex Blumberg, co-reported this story with NPR reporter Adam Davidson.
sentences.zh: 我们的制作人之一亚历克斯·布伦伯格（Alex Blumberg），与NPR记者亚当·戴维森（Adam Davidson）共同报道了这个故事。

sentences.en: The story continues. From 2003 to 2006, the housing market was in a classic speculative bubble.
sentences.zh: 故事继续。从2003年到2006年，房地产市场处于典型的投机泡沫之中。

sentences.en: Home loans were easy to get. So more and more people were buying houses.
sentences.zh: 购房贷款很容易申请。因此越来越多的人开始买房。

sentences.en: The increased demand for houses caused the prices to increase.
sentences.zh: 对房屋需求的增加导致房价上涨。

sentences.en: And the rising prices created even more demand, as people started to look at homes as investments, investments that never went down in value.
sentences.zh: 而不断上涨的房价引发了更大的需求，因为人们开始把房子当作投资，一种价值永远不会下跌的投资。

sentences.en: And in 2003, 2004, 2005 they didn't. You could buy a house with no money down, turn around and sell it a year later for-- in some areas-- double what you paid.
sentences.zh: 在2003年、2004年、2005年确实如此。你买房甚至不需要首付，转手在一年后卖掉——在某些地区——就能卖出你购入价格的两倍。

sentences.en: People who had never invested in real estate before started buying multiple properties as investments.
sentences.zh: 以前从未投资过房地产的人也开始买入多处房产作为投资。

sentences.en: There were even shows on TV about how to do it.
sentences.zh: 电视上甚至还有关于怎么操作这类投资的节目。

sentences.en: Here's a promo. Get ready for an all new season of Flip This House.
sentences.zh: 这是一段宣传片。准备好迎接《翻修这栋房子》（Flip This House）的全新一季吧。

sentences.en: This is A&E's Flip This House. Discovery had the cleverly titled, Flip That House.
sentences.zh: 这是A&E频道的《翻修这栋房子》。Discovery频道也有个名字很巧妙的节目叫《翻新那栋房子》（Flip That House）。

sentences.en: There were other ones-- Property Ladder, Designed to Sell.
sentences.zh: 还有其他的节目——《房地产梯子》（Property Ladder）、《设计待售》（Designed to Sell）。

sentences.en: Bravo came late to the game, debuting their show, Flipping Out, in November of 2007, well after the bubble had already popped.
sentences.zh: Bravo频道入局较晚，他们的节目《操盘手》（Flipping Out）于2007年11月开播，那时泡沫其实早就破裂了。

sentences.en: Those white boys from New Haven, going to flip that kitchen.
sentences.zh: 纽黑文的那些白人小子，准备去翻修那个厨房。

sentences.en: Flip This House premieres Saturday, March 31 at 9:00 on A&E.
sentences.zh: 《翻修这栋房子》将于3月31日周六晚9点在A&E频道首播。

sentences.en: The problem was that even though housing prices were going through the roof, people weren't making any more money.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，尽管房价飞涨，但人们的收入并没有增加。

sentences.en: From 2000 to 2007 the median household income stayed flat.
sentences.zh: 从2000年到2007年，美国家庭收入的中位数一直停滞不前。

sentences.en: And so the more prices rose, the more tenuous the whole thing became.
sentences.zh: 因此，房价涨得越高，整个系统就变得越脆弱。

sentences.en: No matter how lax lending standards got, no matter how many exotic mortgage products were created to shoehorn people into homes they couldn't possibly afford, no matter what the mortgage machine tried, the people just couldn't swing it.
sentences.zh: 无论放贷标准变得多么宽松，无论创造出多少奇奇怪怪的房贷产品去硬塞给那些根本买不起房的人，无论按揭机器怎么努力，老百姓就是搞不定。

sentences.en: By late 2006, the average home cost nearly four times what the average family made.
sentences.zh: 到2006年底，普通房屋的平均价格几乎是普通家庭收入的四倍。

sentences.en: Historically it was between two and three times.
sentences.zh: 历史上这个比例通常在两到三倍之间。

sentences.en: And mortgage lenders started to notice something they had almost never seen before.
sentences.zh: 而抵押贷款放贷机构开始注意到一件他们几乎从未见过的事。

sentences.en: People would close on a house, sign all the papers, and then default on their very first payment.
sentences.zh: 人们买下一套房，把所有的文件都签了，然后就在第一笔还款时就违约了。

sentences.en: No loss of a job, no medical emergency, they were under water before they even started.
sentences.zh: 没有失业，没有突发的医疗紧急情况，他们甚至还没开始就已经陷入绝境了。

sentences.en: And although no one could really hear it, that was probably the moment when one of the biggest speculative bubbles in American history popped.
sentences.zh: 虽然当时几乎没人听到，但那可能正是美国历史上最大的投机泡沫破裂的瞬间。

sentences.en: Strangely, the first people in the mortgage-backed security chain who noticed were the ones near the top, the people on Wall Street like Mike Francis.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，抵押贷款支持证券链条上最先察觉到这一点的人，反而是位于顶端的人，也就是华尔街的那些人，比如迈克·弗朗西斯（Mike Francis）。

sentences.en: He can remember almost to the day. It would be somewhere around Halloween of 2006.
sentences.zh: 他几乎能精确到哪一天。大概就在2006年的万圣节前后。

sentences.en: We started seeing our securities that were even six, seven, eight months old start to perform very, very poorly.
sentences.zh: 我们开始发现，那些只有六个月、七个月、八个月历史的证券，表现开始变得非常非常糟糕。

sentences.en: We started to really dig into the details to figure out what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我们开始深入挖掘细节，想弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And then you start seeing, wow, the property values have stopped increasing.
sentences.zh: 然后你开始发现，哇，房产价值已经停止上涨了。

sentences.en: Something is really turning around bad here.
sentences.zh: 这里面绝对出了大问题。

sentences.en: What do we do? The problem was that once property values started going down, it set off a reverse chain reaction, the opposite of what had been happening in the bubble.
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么办？问题在于，一旦房产价值开始下跌，它就会引发一场逆向的连锁反应，这与泡沫时期发生的情况正好相反。

sentences.en: As more people defaulted, more houses came on the market.
sentences.zh: 随着更多人违约，更多的房子被挂牌出售。

sentences.en: With no buyers, prices went even further down.
sentences.zh: 由于没有买家，房价进一步下跌。

sentences.en: And as prices declined, Mike Francis cleared up a mystery.
sentences.zh: 随着房价下跌，迈克·弗朗西斯解开了一个谜团。

sentences.en: Remember, even though he didn't trust these NINA loans, the bonds he turned them into, they performed well.
sentences.zh: 记住，尽管他并不信任这些NINA（无收入无资产）贷款，但他把这些贷款打包成的债券，之前的表现却一直很好。

sentences.en: Well, there was a reason. It's obvious that they performed well, now, because their property kept increasing in value.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是有原因的。现在看来，它们表现好是很显然的，因为房产的价值一直在上涨。

sentences.en: And over time, they could continue to take cash out of it, if they needed to, to pay the bill.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，如果他们需要钱来付账，他们可以继续从房子里套出现金。

sentences.en: In other words, they could take out another loan from the bank, against the value of their house, which because of the bubble was now worth more than they bought it for.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们可以根据房子的价值从银行再贷一笔款，由于泡沫的存在，房子的价值现在比他们买的时候还要高。

sentences.en: These loans, called home equity lines of credit, became very popular in the early to mid 2000s partly because they were easy to get, but partly because people needed them to continue making their original mortgage payments.
sentences.zh: 这类被称为房屋净值信用额度的贷款，在2000年代初至中期变得非常流行，部分原因是它们很容易申请，但部分原因也是因为人们需要靠它们来继续支付最初的房贷。

sentences.en: To pay off their debts, they went into more debt.
sentences.zh: 为了还清债务，他们背上了更多的债务。

sentences.en: And in late 2006 early 2007-- as prices began their plunge and alarm was spreading across mortgage-backed securities desks all over Wall Street-- the people on Wall Street, like Mike Francis, started backing away from some of the riskiest mortgages that they would accept.
sentences.zh: 在2006年底到2007年初——随着价格开始暴跌，恐慌情绪开始在整个华尔街的抵押贷款支持证券交易台蔓延——华尔街的人，比如迈克·弗朗西斯，开始从他们原本愿意接受的一些风险最高的抵押贷款中抽身。

sentences.en: Which had a devastating effect on the mortgage companies, which had proliferated to sell them loans, a devastating effect on people like Mike Garner, the mortgage banker in Nevada, for one simple reason. (SUBJECT) MIKE GARNER: All these mid-size companies like us, we're not using our own money to fund these loans.
sentences.zh: 这给抵押贷款公司带来了毁灭性的打击，此前为了卖出这些贷款，这类公司如雨后春笋般涌现；这对像内华达州的抵押贷款银行家迈克·加纳（Mike Garner）这样的人也产生了毁灭性的打击，原因很简单。访谈对象 迈克·加纳：所有像我们这样规模的中型公司，我们都不是用自己的钱来资助这些贷款的。

sentences.en: The way it worked was that a small bank, like Silver State Mortgage where Mike Garner worked, would borrow money from a big bank, say Citibank or Washington Mutual.
sentences.zh: 它的运作方式是，像迈克·加纳工作的白银州抵押贷款公司（Silver State Mortgage）这样的小银行，会从花旗银行或华盛顿互惠银行这样的大银行借钱。

sentences.en: Silver State would use this borrowed money to buy up a bunch of loans and then pay back the big bank once it sold the loans to Wall Street.
sentences.zh: 白银州会用这笔借来的钱买下一批贷款，然后在把这些贷款卖给华尔街后，再把钱还给大银行。

sentences.en: Now these smaller banks were highly leveraged, in most cases 20:1.
sentences.zh: 当时这些小银行的杠杆率极高，大多数情况下达到20比1。

sentences.en: Meaning in Silver State's case, even though it had, say, only $5 million of its own dollars, it could borrow 20 times that, $100 million, to buy loans with.
sentences.zh: 这意味着以白银州银行为例，尽管它自己的资金可能只有500万美元左右，但它可以借到其20倍的资金，也就是1亿美元，用来购买贷款。

sentences.en: So in late 2006, Mike is busily at it-- borrowing, buying, selling, paying back, and borrowing again-- when the emails started coming.
sentences.zh: 所以在2006年底，迈克正忙得不可开交——借钱、买入、卖出、还款，然后再借钱——这时邮件开始雪片般飞来。

sentences.en: We get an email from a street firm-- I don't know, just say Credit Suisse First Boston.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了来自一家华尔街公司的邮件——我不知道，就说是瑞士信贷第一波士顿吧。

sentences.en: It says, as of-- whatever date-- December 29, we are no longer buying a stated income loan with a FICO less than whatever.
sentences.zh: 邮件上说，从某某日期——12月29日起，我们不再购买FICO信用评分低于某个数值的声明收入贷款。

sentences.en: And the email would say, there will be no exceptions.
sentences.zh: 邮件还会说，没有任何例外情况。

sentences.en: Please do not call the pricing desk to make any exceptions for this for this, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 请不要打电话给定价部门，要求为此破例，或者诸如此类的话。

sentences.en: So you just start flipping out, and say, wait a second.
sentences.zh: 所以你顿时就慌了神，心想，等一下。

sentences.en: You can't just say that you're not going to buy this with no notice.
sentences.zh: 你们怎么能毫无预兆地说不买就不买呢？

sentences.en: Well, we're saying it. And there is no notice.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们现在就在这么说。而且没有任何预兆。

sentences.en: So, then you start to scramble and get the stuff out the door as soon as you can.
sentences.zh: 于是，你开始手忙脚乱地想尽一切办法尽快把这些货清出去。

sentences.en: Because you've already been assembling a bunch of those loans with those characteristics in play somewhere, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你手里已经攒了一大批带有这些特征、正在审批流程中的贷款了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, you've got $20 million, or whatever the number is, sitting there.
sentences.zh: 对，你手里有2000万美元，或者别的什么数额的贷款，就摆在那里。

sentences.en: And you say, oh crap. Well, I had better get those out the door, because within a week of when one street firm says we're not going to buy these loans, you can pretty much expect to see the same email from all them.
sentences.zh: 然后你说，糟糕透了。好吧，我最好赶紧把这些货甩掉，因为在一家华尔街公司说“我们不买这些贷款”的一周内，你基本上可以预料到所有其他公司也都会发来一模一样的邮件。

sentences.en: A lot of times you'll get it from two others the same day.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，你会在同一天收到另外两家公司的同类邮件。

sentences.en: So you're scrambling to sell them. And you're just going off sheer relationships you have with these guys.
sentences.zh: 所以你手忙脚乱地想把它们卖出去。你只能完全依靠你和这些家伙之间的私人交情。

sentences.en: Like, OK, I've still got $10 million of these.
sentences.zh: 比如，好吧，我手里还有1000万这种贷款。

sentences.en: I know you're not buying them anymore, but you've got to.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们不买这玩意儿了，但你们无论如何得接盘。

sentences.en: Come on, you can't just leave me like this.
sentences.zh: 拜托，你们不能就这么把我晾在这儿啊。

sentences.en: But there comes a point where-- well, there came a point where, basically, all of them just said, we're not buying anything.
sentences.zh: 但总会到一个时候——好吧，确实到了这样一个时刻，基本上，所有这些公司都直截了当地说：我们什么都不买。

sentences.en: For Mike and his company that meant that they'd borrowed tens of millions of dollars to buy loans that now they couldn't sell.
sentences.zh: 对迈克和他的公司来说，这意味着他们借了几千万美元买来的贷款，现在根本卖不出去了。

sentences.en: And since they had very little of their own money-- just like the home buyers whose mortgages they purchased-- they had no choice but to default on their loan.
sentences.zh: 由于他们自己几乎没什么钱——就像那些购买了房贷的购房者一样——他们别无选择，只能面临贷款违约。

sentences.en: Silver State Mortgage's nearly 600 employees were out of work quite suddenly.
sentences.zh: 白银州抵押贷款公司近600名员工非常突然地失业了。

sentences.en: It was February 14. The email went out and said, Silver State Mortgage might be going out of business, but-- It was something along these lines-- might be going out of business, but we think we can work something out.
sentences.zh: 那是2月14日。邮件发了出来，上面说，白银州抵押贷款公司可能会倒闭，但是——大致是这个意思——可能会倒闭，但我们觉得我们还能商量出一个解决方案。

sentences.en: So we would encourage you to please come in and work tomorrow, and give us one more day to see if we can work something out.
sentences.zh: 所以我们鼓励大家明天照常来上班，再给我们一天时间，看能不能谈出个结果。

sentences.en: And the next day people came in. And the email went out and said, unfortunately, we were not able to work anything out.
sentences.zh: 第二天大家来上班了。然后邮件又发出来了，上面说，不幸的是，我们没能谈成任何解决方案。

sentences.en: So Silver State Mortgage will be closing our doors today.
sentences.zh: 所以白银州抵押贷款公司今天将正式关门大吉。

sentences.en: And that's how most of these lenders go under.
sentences.zh: 大多数这样的放贷机构就是这样倒闭的。

sentences.en: Everybody was working, thinking everything's great, chugging along.
sentences.zh: 大家本来都在工作，觉得一切都好得很，顺风顺水地往前开。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, the bank says, you're done.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，银行发话了：你们完蛋了。

sentences.en: Then people starting grabbing their computers and their copy machines and rolling them out of the building.
sentences.zh: 然后人们开始抢搬他们的电脑和复印机，把它们滚出大楼。

sentences.en: It was a mess.
sentences.zh: 那一团糟。

sentences.en: My thoughts were like, holy crap. Everybody's just stealing all their stuff.
sentences.zh: 我当时的内心独白就像是，天哪。所有人都在疯狂偷公司里的东西。

sentences.en: That happened on February 14? Yep.
sentences.zh: 那是2月14日发生的？没错。

sentences.en: My boss calls it the Valentine's Day Massacre.
sentences.zh: 我老板把它叫做“情人节大屠杀”。

sentences.en: For Glen Pizzolorusso, the mortgage sales manager who-- not to dwell on this detail-- was living the life of a B-list celebrity, the end came a little more slowly.
sentences.zh: 对于Glen Pizzolorusso这位抵押贷款销售经理来说——话不要说得太满——他之前过着二线名人的生活，而他的结局则来得稍微缓慢一些。

sentences.en: So you're at WMC.
sentences.zh: 所以你当时在WMC公司。

sentences.en: What was the turning point?
sentences.zh: 转折点是什么时候？

sentences.en: I mean this sounds obscene, but I think it was the first month I got a $25,000 paycheck.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是这听起来可能有点荒唐，但我觉得就是我拿到25000美元月薪的那第一个月。

sentences.en: And at this time, that didn't cover my expenses.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这点钱甚至还不够支付我的开销。

sentences.en: So you're sitting here, and you're like, I just made $25,000 this month, which is more than most people make in six months, and it doesn't even cover my expenses.
sentences.zh: 所以你坐在那儿，心想，我这个月刚赚了25000美元，这比大多数人半年赚的还要多，但它甚至都不够付我的账单。

sentences.en: Now what do I do?
sentences.zh: 那我接下来该怎么办？

sentences.en: And then the next couple months I made like $30,000 or $40,000.
sentences.zh: 然后接下来的几个月，我赚了大概30000或40000美元。

sentences.en: And then it went down to $10,000. You could just feel it winding down.
sentences.zh: 接着收入降到了10000美元。你简直能清晰地感觉到它在一步步走向衰亡。

sentences.en: You knew the good old days were over. And it was scary.
sentences.zh: 你知道好日子一去不复返了。这让人感到害怕。

sentences.en: So give me your situation now. Like, can you pay all your bills now?
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲你现在的情况吧。比如，你现在能付清所有的账单吗？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 说实话不能。

sentences.en: I borrowed some money from some friends-- well, not-- from my dad.
sentences.zh: 我从一些朋友那里借了点钱——哦不，是从我爸那儿借的。

sentences.en: Borrowed some money from Dad. I'm living in my house right now.
sentences.zh: 从我爸那儿借了点钱。我现在就住在我的房子里。

sentences.en: We're working with the bank to try to avoid foreclosure.
sentences.zh: 我们正在跟银行协商，希望能避免房屋被止赎。

sentences.en: At this point, I'm dealing with an attorney.
sentences.zh: 目前，我在和一个律师打交道。

sentences.en: I'm trying to figure out if it makes sense for me to just walk away from the house.
sentences.zh: 我正在琢磨，我是不是直接放弃这套房子算了。

sentences.en: And have you been making mortgage payments or not?
sentences.zh: 那你最近一直在按时还房贷吗？

sentences.en: No. When was the last time you made a mortgage payment?
sentences.zh: 没有。你上次交房贷是什么时候？

sentences.en: January, maybe.
sentences.zh: 大概是一月份吧。

sentences.en: And I've been just making them spotty, as I can, just enough to keep them off my back.
sentences.zh: 我一直都是东拼凑凑、断断续续地还，只要手头有就还一点，勉强能让催收的不来纠缠我。

sentences.en: I mean, I have to watch every penny right now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我现在每一分钱都得精打细算。

sentences.en: As you can see, this is my living room. I have no furniture in there, because, like I said, it's either buy furniture or pay my mortgage.
sentences.zh: 如你所见，这就是我的客厅。里面没有任何家具，因为就像我说的，要嘛买家具，要嘛交房贷。

sentences.en: This brings us back to Richard, the marine we met at the very top of the show.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带回了理查德（Richard），我们在节目开头见到的那个海军陆战队员。

sentences.en: He, like more than 4 million Americans at this point, is fighting to keep his home.
sentences.zh: 此时此刻，他和超过450万美国人一样，正在为保住自己的家而苦苦抗争。

sentences.en: He's giving me a tour. And I wanted to talk to him about, what now?
sentences.zh: 他正在带我参观。我想跟他聊聊，接下来怎么办？

sentences.en: What happens next, now that the housing bubble has turned into a crisis?
sentences.zh: 既然房地产泡沫已经演变成了一场危机，接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: If he defaults on his mortgage, nobody wins.
sentences.zh: 如果他的房贷违约，没有人是赢家。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to leave his house. The investors who own his mortgage, the last thing they want is to own a house in east Flatbush in a declining market with no buyers.
sentences.zh: 他不想离开自己的房子。拥有他房贷的投资者，最不愿意看到的就是在房价下跌、没有买家的市场里，手里多出一栋位于东弗拉特布什（east Flatbush）的房子。

sentences.en: So you think it would be easy for both sides to come together and modify Richard's mortgage, figure out something he can afford.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会觉得，双方坐下来协商并修改理查德的房贷、找出一个他能负担得起的方案，应该是件很简单的事。

sentences.en: You'd be wrong.
sentences.zh: 那你就大错特错了。

sentences.en: Kerry Campbell, nice to meet you. Good, how you doing sir?
sentences.zh: 凯瑞·坎贝尔（Kerry Campbell），很高兴认识你。很好，你好啊先生。

sentences.en: The offices of NACA, the Neighborhood Assistance Corporation of America in Newark, New Jersey are short on frills.
sentences.zh: 位于新泽西州纽瓦克的美国国家住房援助公司（NACA）的办公室没有什么华丽的装潢。

sentences.en: Kerry Campbell, who's helping Richard today, is a counselor here.
sentences.zh: 今天负责帮助理查德的凯瑞·坎贝尔是这里的咨询师。

sentences.en: The goal today is to figure out how big a mortgage payment Richard can actually afford to pay.
sentences.zh: 今天的目标是搞清楚理查德实际上到底能负担得起多大的房贷月供。

sentences.en: So Kerry needs to know everything Richard spends money on.
sentences.zh: 所以凯瑞需要了解理查德花钱的方方面面。

sentences.en: They go through his medical bills, his clothing budget.
sentences.zh: 他们仔细核对他的医疗账单、服装预算。

sentences.en: Kerry gently nudges Richard to be realistic, like when he asks Richard how much he spends on gifts for his family.
sentences.zh: 凯瑞温和地提醒理查德要切合实际，比如当他问理查德花在给家人买礼物上的钱有多少时。

sentences.en: Gifts for family, how much would you say on average? $300 at Christmas time.
sentences.zh: 给家人的礼物，你觉得平均大概是多少？圣诞节的时候大概300美元。

sentences.en: January, February-- January through December, Mother's day, Father's day, sisters, brothers, nephews, nieces, significant other, kid's birthday, if you celebrate Christmas-- whole enchilada.
sentences.zh: 一月、二月——从一月到十二月，母亲节、父亲节、姐妹、兄弟、侄子、外甥、另一半、孩子的生日，如果你庆祝圣诞节的话——全部加起来。

sentences.en: That sounds about right. The process we're doing right now, how does this compare to when you bought the house?
sentences.zh: 听起来差不多就是这样。我们现在做的这个流程，跟你当年买房的时候相比怎么样？

sentences.en: This is totally different. It's brand new to me.
sentences.zh: 这完全不一样。对我来说是全新体验。

sentences.en: But when I bought my house it was just your credit score and can I pull a credit report?
sentences.zh: 但我买房的时候，他们就只看你的信用评分，看我能不能拉出一份信用报告。

sentences.en: So in this whole process, what's the first time someone looked at your finances?
sentences.zh: 所以在整个购房过程中，历史上第一次有人真正审查你的财务状况是什么时候？

sentences.en: Today. Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。就在今天。

sentences.en: Not to say the original broker didn't have a process.
sentences.zh: 并不是说当年的那个中介没有走什么流程。

sentences.en: It just had nothing to do with reality. Kerry shows Richard the loan documents filled out when he bought the house by his original broker.
sentences.zh: 只是那套流程跟现实毫无关系。凯瑞向理查德展示了当年他买房时，由他最初的经办中介填写的一份贷款文件。

sentences.en: Here it's saying your base employment income was $16,250 a month.
sentences.zh: 上面写着你当时的基本就业收入是每月16250美元。

sentences.en: What? $16,250 a month, which means your salary on a yearly basis would be making-- you're making just under $200,000, $195,000 to be exact.
sentences.zh: 什么？每月16250美元，这意味着你的年薪将达到——你每年的收入略低于20万美元，准确地说是195000美元。

sentences.en: I wish.
sentences.zh: 我要是能赚那么多就好了。

sentences.en: In 2005-- and they used my 2005 taxes-- I was making $37,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 在2005年——他们用的是我2005年的纳税申报单——我一年的收入是37000美元。

sentences.en: Did you know that number until now? No. So he stated $16,000 a month.
sentences.zh: 在看到这个数字之前你知道这件事吗？不知道。所以他虚报说我月入1.6万美元。

sentences.en: To me, that is shocking. To you, it's not that shocking?
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这太令人震惊了。对你来说这没那么震惊吗？

sentences.en: Oh, that's outrageous. But it's a common thing.
sentences.zh: 哦，这太离谱了。但这是很常见的情况。

sentences.en: There's worlds apart from the reality and what's on a lot of these documents.
sentences.zh: 现实情况和很多这种文件上写的东西简直有着天壤之别。

sentences.en: Another thing the papers reveal, how much that creative broker made, $18,500.
sentences.zh: 文件还透露了另一件事，那个满脑子花招的中介赚了多少佣金：18500美元。

sentences.en: As Kerry says, that's 18,000 reasons to falsify Richards mortgage documents and to put him in a house he can't afford.
sentences.zh: 正如凯瑞所说，这就是1万8千个去伪造理查德房贷文件、并把他推进一套他根本买不起的房子的绝佳理由。

sentences.en: Richard actually qualified for a Veterans Administration Loan at a really good rate.
sentences.zh: 理查德其实有资格申请退伍军人管理局（VA）的贷款，利率非常优惠。

sentences.en: And he had money to put down. But the broker convinced him to take a mortgage that turned out to be much worse, but did have a much higher commission.
sentences.zh: 而且他当时也有钱支付首付。但中介说服他去贷款买了一套结果证明糟糕得多、但佣金却高得多的房子。

sentences.en: Mortgage brokers were walking around east Flatbush knocking on doors, telling just about anybody, hey, we can get you a house.
sentences.zh: 抵押贷款中介在东弗拉特布什到处敲门，对几乎遇到的任何人说，嘿，我们能帮你买到一套房。

sentences.en: If you have a house, we can get you a big home equity line of credit.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经有了房，我们可以帮你办到一大笔房屋净值信用额度。

sentences.en: This happened in poor neighborhoods all over the country.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的贫困社区都发生了这种事。

sentences.en: And while the FBI and other law enforcement folks say they don't have the exact numbers, it's clear that fraud, like that fraud on Richard's application, was ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 虽然联邦调查局和其他执法人员表示他们没有确切的数字，但很明显，像理查德申请表上那样的欺诈行为可以说是无处不在。

sentences.en: At the end of Richard's budget process, the math they come up with is fairly stark.
sentences.zh: 在理查德的预算流程接近尾声时，他们算出来的数学账目可以说是相当严峻。

sentences.en: Richard makes more money now. He got a new and better job.
sentences.zh: 理查德现在的收入其实更高了。他找了一份更好、崭新的工作。

sentences.en: So he makes an average, before taxes, of $8,000 a month.
sentences.zh: 所以扣除税款前，他平均每月的收入是8000美元。

sentences.en: Which means after taxes he brings home exactly enough to pay his mortgage and nothing else.
sentences.zh: 这意味着扣除税款后，他带回家的钱刚好够付房贷，别的什么都干不了。

sentences.en: All of his living expenses he says, are paid with money he gets from his mom, who is on public assistance, his girlfriend, and his brother.
sentences.zh: 他说，他所有的生活开销都是用他妈妈（吃政府救济的）、他女朋友以及他兄弟给他的钱来支付的。

sentences.en: Kerry runs the software, which says that if Richard is going to stay in his house, he needs a much cheaper mortgage.
sentences.zh: 凯瑞运行了一下软件，软件显示如果理查德想保住他的房子，他就需要一笔便宜得多的房贷。

sentences.en: The interest, which is currently at around 10%, would have to be lowered a lot, to 3%.
sentences.zh: 目前高达10%左右的利率，必须大幅下调，降至3%。

sentences.en: Kerry wants to propose this to whoever owns the loan, but this brings him to this peculiar problem mortgage owners face now.
sentences.zh: 凯瑞想把这个方案提议给这笔贷款的当前所有人，但这让他面临着如今抵押贷款所有者们所面临的一个奇特难题。

sentences.en: They have no idea who that is. Richard's loan has been bought, and sold, and resold, and put into one of those pools owned by investors, maybe an investor like Jim Finkel.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道那个人是谁。理查德的贷款已经被买进卖出、反复转手，并被塞进了由投资者们持有的那些资产池之一，也许这个投资者就是像Jim Finkel这样的人。

sentences.en: 150 times was it 3,000-- let's be conservative?
sentences.zh: 是150次，还是3000次——我们往保守了说？

sentences.en: So, now we're back in Jim Finkel's office.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在我们回到了Jim Finkel的办公室。

sentences.en: He is surrounded by very expensive computers, but he's typing on a cheap calculator.
sentences.zh: 他的周围摆满了价格昂贵的电脑，但他却在一个廉价的计算器上敲敲打打。

sentences.en: And he's trying to figure out for us how many individual mortgages, how many homes like Richard's, does he and his company own a part of.
sentences.zh: 他正试图为我们计算清楚，他和他的公司究竟持有了多少笔独立的抵押贷款、多少套像理查德这样的房子的部分产权。

sentences.en: The calculator method soon fails him, and he turns to one of his number crunchers, a guy named Alex.
sentences.zh: 计算器的方法很快不管用了，他转而向他的一位数码计算专家求助，一个名叫Alex的家伙。

sentences.en: I can't even imagine-- Alex, do you have any idea?
sentences.zh: 我简直无法想象——Alex，你心里有数吗？

sentences.en: Alex gets on the phone with Steve, the IT guy.
sentences.zh: Alex拿起电话打给IT人员Steve。

sentences.en: How many loans are you running in loan performance, altogether?
sentences.zh: 你们在贷款表现系统里总共运行着多少笔贷款？

sentences.en: For all of our deals, how many loans, individual mortgage loans?
sentences.zh: 在我们所有的交易中，一共有多少笔贷款，独立的抵押贷款？

sentences.en: 16 million loans? This one CDO factory, this one office, owns a share of 16 million homes.
sentences.zh: 1600万笔贷款？仅仅这一个CDO工厂、这一个办公室，就持有了1600万套房屋的部分份额。
