sentences.en: And each of these homes has lots of other owners, people in other CDO offices around the world-- there are lots of them-- and other investors.
sentences.zh: 而这其中的每一套房子，其实还有很多其他的拥有者，也就是世界各地其他CDO办公室的人——这种办公室有很多——以及其他的投资者们。

sentences.en: You start to see what a crazy web of confusing interconnections this whole process is.
sentences.zh: 你开始发现，整个过程交织成了一张多么疯狂、令人头晕目眩的复杂网络。

sentences.en: Now until this moment, we had a theory that the homeowners and the people on the other end, the people at the top of the chain-- The investors-- The investors like Jim Finkel-- That they had no idea about each other.
sentences.zh: 直到这一刻，我们一直有一种理论，认为购房者和处于另一端、位于链条顶端的人—— 投资者们—— 像Jim Finkel这样的投资者们—— 他们对彼此一无所知。

sentences.en: Right, but we actually learned that they know quite a lot about each other.
sentences.zh: 对，但实际上我们了解到，他们对彼此相当了解。

sentences.en: They just see each other through a computer screen.
sentences.zh: 他们只是通过电脑屏幕来看待对方。

sentences.en: Hey, Steve. We find that out when we go downstairs to see Steve Pennington, the IT guy.
sentences.zh: 嘿，Steve。当我们下楼去找负责IT的技术人员Steve Pennington时，我们发现了这一点。

sentences.en: Steve's actual title is head of financial engineering.
sentences.zh: Steve的实际头衔是金融工程负责人。

sentences.en: He's created his own software program that actually looks at every one of the 16 million loans Dynamic owns part of.
sentences.zh: 他自己开发了一套软件程序，能够实际查看Dynamic公司持有的全部1600万笔贷款中的每一笔。

sentences.en: It's a spreadsheet. Each line is one loan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个电子表格。每一行代表一笔贷款。

sentences.en: And it has all sorts of information like how much the house sold for, what the interest rate is.
sentences.zh: 上面有各种各样的信息，比如房子是以多少价格卖出的、利率是多少。

sentences.en: He points to one field, which is the most baffling one.
sentences.zh: 他指着其中一个栏目，这是最令人感到匪夷所思的一个。

sentences.en: It's just a cell on a spreadsheet. And it just has 12 letters and numbers in a row.
sentences.zh: 那只是电子表格里的一个单元格。上面只有连续的12个字母和数字。

sentences.en: Every letter represents a month. What does the nine mean?
sentences.zh: 每一个字母代表一个月。那这个“9”是什么意思？

sentences.en: It means they are 90 days of, basically, delinquent on their loan.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们的贷款基本上已经逾期90天了。

sentences.en: So is this the Matrix, where the guy's looking at the green digits passing.
sentences.zh: 所以这难道是《黑客帝国》（The Matrix）吗，那个男的在看着绿色数字滚动。

sentences.en: And he's saying, oh there's the redhead, there's the blond?
sentences.zh: 然后他说，哦，那是红发女郎，那是金发女郎？

sentences.en: Are you, Steve, seeing lives here? I definitely see lives.
sentences.zh: Steve，你在这里看到了鲜活的人生吗？我确实看到了人生。

sentences.en: Especially when you look at this here, this thing here?
sentences.zh: 特别是当你看到这个的时候，这个东西？

sentences.en: That's to me, the most vivid. Just for the record, I see a bunch of-- CCCCC3636CC-- I do not see a human drama.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这是最生动的。为了留下记录，我看到了一堆——CCCCC3636CC——我可没看出什么人类的宏大悲喜剧。

sentences.en: The drama here, is you've got someone who's been paying their loan, and then something's happened.
sentences.zh: 这里的戏剧性在于，你遇到了这样一个人，他之前一直在按时还贷，然后出了点状况。

sentences.en: And then they've gone three months delinquent, three months delinquent, six months delinquent, and then three months.
sentences.zh: 接着他们开始逾期三个月，逾期三个月，逾期六个月，然后又是逾期三个月。

sentences.en: So they basically got to this point of six, and then they fought back the current.
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上陷入了这个长达六个月的困境，然后他们又开始拼命挣扎，试图把逆境扭转过来。

sentences.en: Now that I've learned the code, now that you've taught me the code, I see it.
sentences.zh: 现在我学会了这套密码，既然你教会了我这套密码，我就能看懂了。

sentences.en: Like here, he was on time for a bunch of months.
sentences.zh: 就像这里，他在好几个月里都是按时还款的。

sentences.en: Then he went 30 days, 30 days, 30 days. Then he went two months behind.
sentences.zh: 然后他逾期了30天，30天，30天。接着他落后了两个月。

sentences.en: Then he came back. And now he seems to-- Right, what's really hard about this is then you watch people-- you can watch over these 12 months, people cycle on and off.
sentences.zh: 然后他又追回来了。现在他似乎——没错，这里面真正残酷的地方在于，你会看着人们——你可以在这12个月里看着人们的财务状况陷入恶性循环并不断进出。

sentences.en: You guys are much more sympathetic. And it might be just because we're reporters, and you want to make us think you're good guys, but you're really cold-hearted.
sentences.zh: 你们显得更有同情心。这可能只是因为我们是记者，而你想让我们觉得你们是好人，但实际上你们铁石心肠。

sentences.en: We're human beings. These guys are hurting you.
sentences.zh: 我们也是活生生的人。这些人正在遭受痛苦。

sentences.en: Their irresponsibility is costing you money and work.
sentences.zh: 他们的不负责任正在让你们损失金钱和工作。

sentences.en: That was up to us to think about three years ago.
sentences.zh: 那是三年前我们才需要去操心的事情。

sentences.en: Do you have any anger when you look at this?
sentences.zh: 你看着这些的时候心里会有愤怒吗？

sentences.en: No, not at all. This is pure sadness.
sentences.zh: 没有，一点也没有。这只有纯粹的悲伤。

sentences.en: This is where the partnership of borrowers like Clarence Nathan and investors liked Jim Finkel has ended up.
sentences.zh: 这就是像Clarence Nathan这样的借款人和像Jim Finkel这样的投资者，他们之间的伙伴关系最终的结局。

sentences.en: Tonko Gast estimates that most of the AAA rated mortgage-backed CDOs that the industry created since 2006 are now worth less than half their value.
sentences.zh: Tonko Gast估计，自2006年以来整个行业创造的大多数AAA级抵押贷款支持CDO，现在的价值已经缩水了一半以上。

sentences.en: Some are worth close to 0. But remember, to all the investment managers in the global pool of money who bought them AAA meant safe as government bonds.
sentences.zh: 有些价值甚至接近于零。但请记住，对于全球资金池中所有买下它们的投资经理来说，AAA级意味着像政府债券一样安全。

sentences.en: AAA was called a cash equivalent, money in the bank.
sentences.zh: AAA级曾被称为现金等价物，是存在银行里的真金白银。

sentences.en: It's as if the global pool of money put trillions of dollars in a savings account, came back one year later, and found out that half the money was gone.
sentences.zh: 这就好比全球资金池把数万亿美元存入了储蓄账户，结果一年后回来一看，发现其中一半的钱不翼而飞了。

sentences.en: Or put another way, it's as if the global pool of money thought it was putting trillions of dollars in a savings account, but really half of it was going into a furnace.
sentences.zh: 或者换句话说，这就好比全球资金池以为自己把数万亿美元存进了储蓄账户，但实际上其中一半的钱被直接扔进了焚化炉。

sentences.en: The money is gone, burned up, never to come back.
sentences.zh: 钱没了，烧成了灰烬，再也回不来了。

sentences.en: And that has led to a new term you've been hearing.
sentences.zh: 这就催生了一个你最近经常听到的新词。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe you've noticed that the press and others don't call it a sub-prime housing crisis as much.
sentences.zh: 对，也许你已经注意到，媒体和其他人不再怎么把这称为次贷住房危机了。

sentences.en: They're now calling it a credit crisis. The global pool of money still has no idea how much money they lost, how much went into the furnace.
sentences.zh: 他们现在把它叫做信贷危机。全球资金池仍然不知道他们到底亏了多少钱，究竟有多少钱进了焚化炉。

sentences.en: And because of that, they've totally changed their thinking.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，他们的思维方式彻底改变了。

sentences.en: They used to be obsessed just with getting some kind of profit, any higher interest rate return.
sentences.zh: 他们过去只痴迷于获取某种利润，追求任何更高利率的回报。

sentences.en: Now the global pool of money has the exact opposite obsession.
sentences.zh: 现在，全球资金池有了完全相反的痴迷。

sentences.en: It wants no risk whatsoever. It just wants safety.
sentences.zh: 它不想要任何哪怕一丁点儿的风险。它只想要安全。

sentences.en: Suddenly, those US government treasury bonds-- still near the historic lows of 1% and 2%-- are beautifully attractive because they're safe.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，那些美国国债——虽然仍徘徊在1%和2%的历史低位——变得极具吸引力，因为它们是安全的。

sentences.en: They will never blow up like sub-prime CDOs did.
sentences.zh: 它们绝不会像次贷CDO那样突然爆雷。

sentences.en: The global pool of money is avoiding anything with even the slightest hint of risk.
sentences.zh: 全球资金池正在极力避开任何带有哪怕一丝一毫风险的东西。

sentences.en: And that affects everybody, no matter who you are.
sentences.zh: 这会影响到每一个人，无论你是谁。

sentences.en: It's harder to borrow money to buy a house, or build a factory, or bring your country boldly into the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 现在借钱买房、建厂，或者带领你的国家大步迈入21世纪，都变得比以前更难了。

sentences.en: Take Iceland. A year ago, it was easy for them to borrow billions.
sentences.zh: 以冰岛为例。一年前，他们借几十亿美元还轻而易举。

sentences.en: Now they're seen as too risky. Their central bank has to pay more than 15% interest to get anyone to loan them money.
sentences.zh: 现在他们被视为风险太高。他们的央行不得不支付超过15%的利息，才能让人愿意借钱给他们。

sentences.en: They could do better putting their national debt on a credit card.
sentences.zh: 他们把国家债务刷在信用卡上说不定都比这划算。

sentences.en: Hungary, Kazakhstan, Turkey, they are all in similar situations.
sentences.zh: 匈牙利、哈萨克斯坦、土耳其，它们都处在类似的境地中。

sentences.en: You might have heard about problems in student lending.
sentences.zh: 你可能也听说过学生贷款方面出现的问题。

sentences.en: Companies that needed credit to survive are shutting down.
sentences.zh: 那些需要信贷来维持生存的公司正在纷纷倒闭。

sentences.en: The US expects more than 1.1 million bankruptcies this year, twice the 2006 number.
sentences.zh: 美国预计今年将有超过110万起破产案，是2006年数字的两倍。

sentences.en: This freezing of credit all around the world is something new.
sentences.zh: 全球信贷的这种全面冻结是前所未有的新现象。

sentences.en: The world has never seen anything on this scale.
sentences.zh: 全世界从未见过如此规模的困境。

sentences.en: When the crisis hit last August, central bankers and finance economists couldn't figure out just how bad things might get.
sentences.zh: 去年8月危机爆发时，央行行长和金融经济学家们根本无法预料情况到底会恶化到什么地步。

sentences.en: There is this question people would ask, will things get like the 1930s or the 1970s?
sentences.zh: 当时人们一直在问这样一个问题：情况会变得像20世纪30年代或者70年代那样吗？

sentences.en: There's a real fear that just like in the '30s, hundreds of banks would collapse.
sentences.zh: 人们真的很担心，就像30年代那样，数以百计的银行会倒闭。

sentences.en: There would be massive unemployment. There was talk of a new, Great Depression.
sentences.zh: 将会出现大规模失业。当时甚至有关于新的“大萧条”的议论。

sentences.en: That talk seems to have faded. And there's more talk that the next few years will feel like the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 那种论调似乎已经渐渐平息了。现在更多的讨论是，未来几年感觉会很像20世纪70年代。

sentences.en: There are lots of technical differences between this crisis and Jimmy Carter's malaise.
sentences.zh: 这场危机与吉米·卡特时期的社会滞胀之间有很多技术细节上的差异。

sentences.en: But for the average person it could feel the same.
sentences.zh: 但对普通人来说，感觉可能会是一样的。

sentences.en: It's not an out-and-out depression. Everything's just kind of crappy.
sentences.zh: 这并不是一场彻底的经济大萧条。一切只是变得非常糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: And not just in housing and banking, but for the economy as a whole.
sentences.zh: 不仅在房地产和银行业，对整个宏观经济来说都是如此。

sentences.en: It's barely growing. There aren't a lot of new businesses, new jobs, unemployment keeps creeping up.
sentences.zh: 经济几乎没有增长。没有出现很多新企业、新工作岗位，失业率一直在悄悄攀升。

sentences.en: We're just sort of stuck in neutral for a while.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在空挡期卡壳了一段时间。

sentences.en: Anyone under, say, 45 probably doesn't remember that 1970s malaise too well.
sentences.zh: 任何年龄在45岁以下的人，大概对70年代那种滞胀 malaise 没有太深刻的记忆。

sentences.en: Anyone under 30 has barely known a US economy that wasn't growing.
sentences.zh: 任何30岁以下的人，几乎从未经历过美国经济不增长的时期。

sentences.en: Now, there's a decent chance we'll all get to see what life felt like in the '70s, which isn't great.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们有相当大的概率能亲身体验一下70年代的生活是什么滋味，这可不是什么好体验。

sentences.en: It's pretty bad, actually, unless you're comparing it to the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 实际上相当糟糕，除非你拿它去和30世纪30年代作对比。

sentences.en: Alex Blumberg and Adam Davidson. Alex, my voice is so bad, I think maybe you should read the credits.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·布伦伯格和亚当·戴维森。亚历克斯，我的嗓子实在太糟糕了，我觉得也许你该来念鸣谢名单。

sentences.en: Why don't you do it? All right, Ira. I hope you feel better.
sentences.zh: 要不你来？好吧，伊拉。祝你早日康复。

sentences.en: I'm going to bring Adam in here to help me to, since I've never done this before.
sentences.zh: 我把亚当请到这儿来帮我一把，因为我以前从来没干过这行。

sentences.en: Thanks today to Ellen Weiss at NPR who made this collaboration happen this week between the news division at NPR, where I work, All Things Considered, and This American Life.
sentences.zh: 感谢今天NPR的埃伦·韦斯（Ellen Weiss），正是她促成了本周我工作的NPR新闻部旗下栏目《所有事情考虑》（All Things Considered）与《美国生活》之间的这次合作。

sentences.zh: 我工作的栏目。还要感谢玛丽·安·卡萨万特（Mary Ann Casavant）、安娜·柴（Anna Chai）、凯文·拜尔斯（Kevin Byers）、出色的住房博客“计算风险”（Calculated Risk）、亚历克西斯·格雷内尔（Alexis Grenell）、斯蒂芬妮·科恩·格拉斯（Stephanie Cohen Glass）、萨吉夫·汉达（Sanjeev Handa）、查理·莱德利（Charlie Ledley）、詹姆斯·斯库洛克（James Scurlock）、克里斯·特平（Chris Turpin）、伊莱恩·格利克（Elaine Glick）、马克·丹·纳伊格罗（Mark Dan Naygrow）。

sentences.zh: 《美国生活》由国际公共广播电台（Public Radio International）发行。

sentences.en: WBEZ management oversight-- No, I want to do this one.
sentences.zh: WBEZ管理监督——不，这一句我想自己来。

sentences.en: OK, here you go. WBEZ management oversight for our program by Ira's boss Mr.
sentences.zh: 好吧，给你。我们节目由伊拉的老板托雷·马拉蒂亚先生进行WBEZ管理监督。

sentences.en: Torey Malatia. He and Ira go out at night sometimes together.
sentences.zh: 他和伊拉有时候晚上会一起出去玩。

sentences.en: It's pretty chill. Torey describes it like this-- You know, we order probably three or four bottles of Cristal at a $1,000 a bottle.
sentences.zh: 挺轻松的。托雷是这么形容的——你知道的，我们大概会点三四瓶水晶香槟，每瓶1000美元。

sentences.en: Everybody's like, whoa, who's the cool guys?
sentences.zh: 大家都在想，哇，这两个酷家伙是谁啊？

sentences.en: I'm not Ira Glass. I'm not either. But we will be back next week with more stories of This American Life.
sentences.zh: 我不是伊拉·格拉斯。我也不是。但我们下周会带着更多《美国生活》的故事准时回归。

sentences.zh: PRI。国际公共广播电台。
